title: A branch-and-filter method for mixed-integer linear programming
abstract: We develop a new tree-search framework for mixed-integer linear programming problems, which incorporates a filter mechanism as a node-acceptance device. The introduced branch-and-filter algorithm combines proper branching actions with a filter on integrality violation and an incumbent-dependent objective coordinate. Inspired by classical filter methods in nonconvex constrained optimization, the proposed method moves to a restoration phase whenever sufficient progress cannot be provided by the filter and funnel mechanisms, the latter of which is anchored at global relaxation lower bounds. Under mild assumptions, the introduced method either certifies infeasibility in finitely many iterations, or converges to global optimality. Moreover, we establish a total outer iteration complexity bound of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ to certification of an $\varepsilon$-optimal mixed-integer solution through fixed-integer linear programming recovery. We finally perform several numerical experiments to study the performance of branch-and-filter against benchmark solvers, under a branch-and-bound, a branch-and-cut, and a novel cell-deletion realization of the proposed restoration oracle.

title: Covariance-Informed Ensemble Score Filtering: Embedding Localized Covariance Geometry into Score-Based Transport
abstract: Background-error covariance models are central to atmospheric data assimilation because they spread partial observational information across space, variables, and dynamically coupled scales. Ensemble and variational methods exploit this covariance geometry efficiently, but their standard analysis formulations are largely built around Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations. Score-based ensemble filtering provides a framework for nonlinear distributional transport, but existing Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) formulations lack an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components. We introduce a covariance-informed ensemble score filter (CI-EnSF) that embeds localized forecast-error covariance geometry directly into the forward diffusion and reverse transport. The proposed forward diffusion is covariance-shaped in standardized state space and becomes isotropic under the corresponding control-variable transformation. This covariance structure continuously propagates observational information from observed to unobserved state components throughout the reverse transport analysis trajectory. Experiments with Lorenz-96 and surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) dynamics show a clear regime dependence. For linear observations, a well-tuned LETKF is more accurate, while CI-EnSF maintains stable cycling and effective covariance-mediated information propagation. Under strongly nonlinear observations and under climatological initialization, CI-EnSF achieves lower analysis error and greater cycling robustness than Gaussian ensemble benchmarks such as the LETKF, with improvements extending across spatial scales in the nonlinear SQG experiment. These results suggest that the principal benefit of CI-EnSF arises from combining nonlinear distributional transport with the mature covariance geometry used in conventional data assimilation.

title: Dirac eigenvalues and the hyper-hemispherical radius
abstract: On a connected compact Riemannian spin manifold with boundary, we prove an upper estimate for the smallest eigenvalue of the Dirac operator under the boundary condition associated with a chirality operator. This upper bound is expressed in terms of the hyper-hemispherical radius. Moreover, the upper bound is realized if and only if the manifold is a hemisphere. As an application, we get a scalar curvature rigidity result for the hemisphere in the case of Lipschitz maps whose differential has a prescribed trace-norm bound. Our estimate extends Bär's result for closed manifolds, where the upper bound is given in terms of hyperspherical radius.

title: Well-posedness for $p(x)$-Laplacian parabolic equations under a multiple-regime setting on an annulus
abstract: This paper proposes an energy-variational framework for the well-posedness of the initial boundary value problem of the parabolic equation with variable exponents on an annulus, under the multiple-regime setting consisting of the subcritical, critical and supercritical regimes of the variable exponents. The multiple-regime setting leads to the appearance of the critical and supercritical regions of positive measure, which cause the failure of the classical Sobolev embedding and the lack of compactness. To address the challenges posed by multiple regimes to well-posedness within the energy framework, we recover the compact Sobolev embedding for a class of radially symmetric functions by the Strauss inequality and obtain the local existence of the solution via the combination of the subdifferential technique and the Principle of Symmetric Criticality for any given radially symmetric initial data. Additionally, the uniqueness result is also given with the recovered Sobolev embedding. Moreover, examining the impact on well-posedness of solutions caused by the variable exponents crossing three sensitive regions, we establish a variational structure of the potential well theory for the evolution equation under the multiple-regime setting on the annulus. For subcritical and critical initial energy levels, we consider the non-positive and positive initial energy cases separately. We obtain the finite-time blow-up of the solution with non-positive initial energy and the threshold condition for global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution with positive initial energy. For supercritical initial energy level, several sufficient criteria for the global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution are given. Finally, the above results, including global existence and finite-time blow-up, are generalized to a more general locally symmetric domain containing an annulus.

title: Group Actions on Aspherical Alexandrov Spaces
abstract: Conner and Raymond proved that if a connected, compact Lie group $G$ acts effectively on a closed aspherical manifold $M$, then $G$ is a torus and the fundamental group of $G$ injects into the center of $π_1(M)$. We prove the corresponding result for effective isometric actions on closed, aspherical Alexandrov spaces.

title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
abstract: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

title: Tropical cohomology for band schemes over the tropical hyperfield
abstract: We define tropical band varieties as $\mathbf{T}$-reductions of separated finitely presented $\mathbf{T}$-band schemes. We construct a faithful functor from the category of tropical band varieties to the category of extended polyhedral spaces in the sense of Gross--Shokrieh. As a byproduct, we show that tropical cohomology can be defined functorially on tropical band varieties.

title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method for Nonsmooth Optimization in the absence of Smooth Surrogates
abstract: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.

title: Swapping Compatible Words
abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality iff $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. In 2024 Carrigan et. al. asked if there is a "natural" bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a "natural" bijection $Φ$ from the set of all finite words to itself such that a word $Ω$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $Φ(Ω)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $Ω$ into $Φ(Ω)$.

title: Profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two
abstract: In this paper, we classify profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two, providing profinite versions of theorems due to Heineken and to Mahdavianary. We also establish that if G is a finitely generated periodic pro-π group, where π is a finite set of odd primes, and all its procyclic subgroups are subnormal of defect at most 2, then G is a finite π-group in which every abelian subgroup is subnormal of defect at most 2.

title: Observability from measurable sets for strongly coupled parabolic systems
abstract: We characterize observability of strongly coupled parabolic systems from arbitrary space-time measurable sets of positive measure. For constant coercive diffusion matrices and arbitrary constant zeroth-order coupling and observation matrices, observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue. The diffusion matrix need not be diagonalizable, and the number of components is arbitrary. The observation is measured in $L^1$, yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality. The proof combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials with a quantitative analysis of the mode-dependent Kalman condition. The resulting finite-dimensional observability estimate is uniform over the spatial modes up to a polynomial frequency loss. A spectral inequality and the Lebeau--Robbiano strategy then give observability of the full system.

title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
abstract: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $ζ_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,dζ_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $ζ_{A,B}$ to Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

title: Research profiles and the mathematical landscape: A grassroots proposal for mathematics with AI
abstract: Repeated mathematical work with AI leaves behind corrections, failed arguments, and sometimes useful ways of asking questions. I propose keeping these in a research profile that the mathematician develops and controls. The profile marks parts of the mathematical landscape according to the researcher's understanding and makes those markings available to later work with AI. This suggests experiments with individual profiles, shared readings of papers, and graduate education. It also raises mathematical questions about the landscape itself: its connections, distances, and changes under discovery. I describe two examples, searching for branches of mathematics with a common base and recovering useful questions from the history of Floer theory. The aim is to give mathematicians something to try and a part in deciding how mathematical AI develops.

title: Quasideterminants and differential realizations of W-algebras
abstract: In this work, we study the Hamiltonian reduction, used in constructing finite rectangular $W$-algebras, of the big-cell differential realization of $\mathfrak{gl}_{np}$. We establish an intrinsic factorization of the reduced differential realization, identifying its Yangian action with the coproduct action on a tensor product of $n$ evaluation differential realizations of $\mathfrak{gl}_p$. Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism through which Hamiltonian reduction transforms the higher-rank differential realization into a factorized lower-rank Yangian action.

title: Random Cellular Automata and deBruijn Graphs
abstract: Update rules of a one dimensional Cellular Automaton can be expressed using an edge-labeled deBruijn graph. We explore various questions about the image of a cellular automaton given by a randomly selected update rule by considering a random deBruijn graph.

title: Tilting theory on continuous quivers (I) maximal rigid and tilting subcategories
abstract: Let $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ be the category of finitely generated persistence modules on the interval $\mathbb I\subseteq\mathbb R$. We study the maximal rigid subcategories of $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$. Maximal rigid interval consistent subcategories are classified via tilting modules over the corresponding discrete type $A$ quiver. We compare several related notions, (weak) tilting and maximal rigidity, in both the context of hereditary abelian categories with enough projective objects and $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ and prove that every maximal rigid interval consistent subcategory is weak tilting and every maximal rigid consistent below subcategory is tilting. We also establish a continuous analogue of Ingalls-Thomas's bijection by showing a bijection between integrally supported maximal rigid consistent below subcategories and integrally generated torsion classes.

title: The $d$-invariant of surgeries on $2$-component L-space links
abstract: Gorsky, B. Liu and Moore provided a formula for the $d$-invariants of integral surgeries on $2$-component $L$-space links with linking number $0$. This paper generalizes these results to the nonzero linking number case. We describe how the $d$-invariant depends on the definiteness of the framing matrix and provide formulae for certain families of positive definite framings, as well as a skein relation for non-algebraically split links.

title: Presheaf structures governed by oriented matroids and pseudohyperplane arrangements
abstract: We study higher complements of pseudohyperplane arrangements and the specialization maps between them, induced by degenerations. We develop a presheaf formalism on oriented matroids and weak maps, which model degenerations. Our main constructions are the posets of weighted and weightwise topes, which provide functorial combinatorial models for higher complements and their specialization morphisms. Their presheaf structure yields a deletion-contraction homotopy pushout, from which we derive a uniform combinatorial proof of the integral cohomology presentation for all $n \geq 2$. This presentation is natural with respect to weak maps and identifies cohomology rings with higher Orlik-Solomon algebras extending the known formulas for linear arrangements to non-realizable oriented matroids. Finally, we equip Deligne groupoids with a presheaf structure and identify them functorially with the fundamental groupoids of the complexified complements.

title: The Strength of Root Cuts in an Extended Abstract Branch-and-Cut Model
abstract: The branch-and-cut paradigm has led to effective solvers for a wide range of mathematical optimization problems. Despite significant theoretical work on pure branching and pure cutting, less is known about their interaction. We study an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to investigate tradeoffs between branching and cutting, including the time to generate cuts. We prove that, under symmetric branching, some minimal-time tree has all cuts at the root, before the first branching node, and that there is an asymmetric setting where some minimal-time tree has no internal cuts, i.e., cuts both preceded and followed by branching. For other settings, although a root-cut tree may be suboptimal and differ substantially in structure from a minimal-time tree, it nevertheless provides a reliable approximation whose tree time does not deviate arbitrarily from the optimum. For constant cut strength and bounded time functions, we show that the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows. In addition, under a single-cut-per-path restriction, we characterize when some minimal-time tree has an internal cut. Lastly, simulations indicate that the best root-cut tree is much closer to a minimal-time tree than our worst-case approximation guarantee suggests.

title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
abstract: We describe a new family of Dirichlet L-functions that provably have an unusual value distribution. Experimentally, we find that the L-functions in this family have a significant and previously undetected bias in the distribution of gaps between their zeros. These phenomena appear to have an arithmetic explanation that corresponds to the nonvanishing of a certain Gauss-type sum. We give a complete classification of the characters for which this sum is nonzero and count them. This sum vanishes for 100% of primitive Dirichlet characters, so L-functions in our newly discovered family are rare (a set of density zero among all primitive characters). The nonvanishing of this sum implies that there is a main term when one integrates the Z-function associated to a Dirichlet L-function over a long interval. We prove that the L-functions in this family are the only GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q cuspidal automorphic L-functions whose Z-functions have a "large" mean value when integrated. We discuss analogous results for the Riemann zeta-function.

title: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension $2n$ with $n+1$ a prime number, and all powers of these varieties. For any variety $X$ of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4, we show that the Lefschetz standard conjecture for $X$ implies the Hodge conjecture for $X$ and all its powers.

title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.

title: Sub-Laplacian Comparison Theorem and Gradient Estimates on Complete Noncompact Contact Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we first derive the Bochner-type formulas of the Hermitian-Tanno connection on contact Riemannian manifolds. Second, we prove a sub-Laplacian comparison theorem on complete noncompact contact Riemannian manifolds with bounded geometric conditions. Finally, we obtain the gradient estimates of a positive eigenfunction on a complete noncompact contact Riemannian manifold which satisfies similar geometric conditions.

title: Pinned configuration sets and slicing theorems via Fourier integral operators
abstract:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_X}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_Y}$ be open, where $d_X,d_Y\geq2$ and $1\leq p\leq\min\{d_X,d_Y\}$. Let $Φ:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^p$ be a smooth mapping, and suppose that $D_xΦ$ and $D_yΦ$ have rank $p$. For compact sets $A\subset X$ and $B\subset Y$, we give lower bounds on $\dim_H A+\dim_H B$ ensuring that the pinned configuration set \[Δ_Φ^y(A)=\{Φ(x,y):x\in A\}\] has positive Lebesgue measure or nonempty interior for some $y\in B$. The dimensional thresholds are expressed in terms of uniform $L^2$-Sobolev estimates for the generalized Radon transforms associated with $Φ$. Our results extend the Fourier integral operator approach developed by Greenleaf, Iosevich, and Taylor for unpinned $2$-point configuration problems to the pinned setting.
  We also prove a nonlinear projection theorem that remains valid even when the Peres-Schlag transversality condition fails. Under the smoothing hypotheses used for the pinned configuration theorem, we obtain lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions of the corresponding slices of $A$ by the level sets of $Φ$. Applications include distances from points to hyperplanes, spheres and lines; multiparameter distance sets; and a restricted projection family introduced by Harris.

title: Displacement structure and eigenvalue bounds for multiband prolate matrices
abstract:
We obtain explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the eigenvalue transition of multiband prolate matrices. Let $S\subset[-1/2,1/2]$ be a finite union of pairwise disjoint intervals, and let $λ_0\ge\cdots\geλ_{N-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $B_{N,S}$. If $ν$ is the number of boundary points of $S$ on the frequency torus, then, for every $0<\eps<1/2$, \[ \#\{k:\eps<λ_k<1-\eps\} \le ν\ceil{\frac{\log(4N)}{π^2} \log\!\left(\frac{4}{\eps(1-\eps)}\right)}. \] Compared with the multiband estimate of Zhu and Wakin~\cite{wakin2017approximating}, this improves the dependence on $\eps$ from order $1/[\eps(1-\eps)]$ to logarithmic dependence. We also prove a second bound in which the main logarithmic term depends on the time--bandwidth product $N|S|$ rather than only on $N$.
  We also compare $S$ with frequency sets having fewer boundary points. Using a classical large-sieve estimate, we take into account not only the total size of the change in the frequency set, but also how that change is distributed. For sets with many small gaps, this can give a bound growing like $\log N$ for fixed $\eps$, even when the bounds based only on the total size of the gaps grow at least linearly in $N$. We also obtain exponential bounds for individual eigenvalues and use them to estimate the error in approximating sampled multiband signals by leading eigenvectors. A discretization argument gives corresponding results for the continuous problem. Numerical examples compare the bounds and examine how the locations of the frequency intervals affect the eigenvalues.

title: Global regularity for 3D large spherically symmetric degenerate compressible Navier-Stokes equations with superlinear BD viscosity and far-field vacuum
abstract: Superlinear density-dependent viscosity presents a fundamental obstacle of global regularity to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the presence of far-field vacuum: the viscous diffusion vanishes at infinity, so excluding vacuum on bounded sets does not suffice to control the flow globally. For $α\in (1,11.7)$ and $γ\in [2α-1,3α-1)$ , we establish global regularity for arbitrarily large, strong, finite-mass initial data with positive density at every finite point and vacuum at infinity. First, we introduce new rescalsed variables regarding the velocity, effective velocity and mass, then we exploit several novel quantities near the center and employ a refined maximum principle to establish the Lipschitz continuity of the velocity at the center-thereby resolving the singularity of the velocity gradient. Another key mechanism is a quantitative control of material volume distortion that remains effective in the vacuum tail. Conservative estimates for the physical and effective velocity gradients yield uniformly vanishing exterior variation tails. These estimates identify a material trajectory with small cumulative Jacobian variation and lead to two-sided bounds for the exterior volume Jacobian, making the evolving density comparable to its initial value along particle paths. On spatial scales determined by the initial density, the resulting degenerate equations admit uniform parabolic estimates that recover control of the physical deformation without a global density lower bound. Combined with compact positivity estimates and a one-sided Glaeser inequality, this closes a homogeneous continuation argument without imposing $L^2$-integrability on the density powers themselves. The solutions conserve mass, preserve far-field vacuum, and remain smooth and strictly positive on every compact spacetime cylinder.

title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
abstract: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.

title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.

title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
abstract: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive. This gives rise to a lower bound of the $m-$index of the Ehrhart polynomial.

title: Piecewise $P_2$ finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation
abstract: This paper develops a piecewise $P_2$ finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation. The discrete space imposes continuity of vertex sums on $(d-2)$-faces and of averaged normal derivatives across interior $(d-1)$-faces. A local algebraic characterization of $P_2$ is first established through the unisolvence of an enriched polynomial space and the resulting compatibility conditions. For each interior element, a $3^d$-element patch is then introduced, and the associated homogeneous patch space is shown to be one-dimensional. The corresponding patch functions, extended by zero, form a basis of the global homogeneous discrete space. A local quadratic interpolation operator is further constructed in arbitrary dimensions. Its approximation properties, together with a consistency estimate derived from the weak continuity conditions, lead to the optimal broken $H^2$ error estimate for the biharmonic problem.

title: Optimal Convergence of Quadratic Not-a-Knot Spline Interpolation on Arbitrary Partitions
abstract: The not-a-knot condition provides a simple spline interpolation scheme that requires no derivative data at the endpoints. Whereas the classical not-a-knot scheme using odd-degree splines selects knots that coincide with the data points, this approach does not extend to the even-degree case. In this paper we establish the well-posedness of the not-a-knot interpolation problem for even-degree splines, where knots are selected at midpoints of data values. We then show that the quadratic case, introduced in [M. J. D. Powell, Approximation Theory and Methods, Cambridge University Press, 1981], achieves $\mathcal{O}(h^3)$ convergence for $C^3$ functions on arbitrary partitions without mesh-ratio restrictions. The proof derives a linear system defining the interpolating spline, normalizes the system to bound the matrix norm of its inverse using a Neumann-series argument, and establishes global error bounds.

title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

title: A Kallin's lemma for polynomials with exponents in a compact convex set and local approximation
abstract: Let $S\subset\Bbb R_+^n$ be compact and convex with $0\in S$, and let $\mathcal{P}^S$ be the algebra spanned by monomials with exponents in $\bigcup_{m\ge0}(mS\cap\Bbb N_0^n)$. We define the associated polynomial hull and prove a Kallin lemma for the union of two sets convex with respect to this algebra. A weighted approximation lemma then shows that, under a sector or ray condition, two admissible monomials generate exactly the functions of the unrestricted algebra that are constant on a specified zero fibre. Applications include an exact density criterion for mixed monomials, a transfer principle for relative perturbations, and density and hull computations on stars of totally real discs.

title: Fisher Information and the Minimum Mean-Square Error for Locating Closely Spaced Point Sources
abstract: We determine the optimal average error of locating closely spaced sources from noisy superpositions of a known smooth response with unknown complex coefficients. Relative phases control how changes in one location can be offset by the other unknowns, so local Fisher information alone does not determine the attainable error. For every fixed number $K\ge2$ of sources with independent uniform phases, we prove matching Bayes risk bounds jointly in separation and noise, for all sufficiently small separations and all noise levels. Odd source counts have two risk regimes; even counts have an intermediate regime in which mean squared error is linear in the noise standard deviation. A projected least-squares estimator attains these orders without knowing the phases or the prior density. Bounded nonuniform phase laws preserve the orders under stated support conditions, whereas priors concentrated near poorly identified configurations can change the exponents. A common finite comparison yields both a global inverse bound and paths controlled by the original prior. These give sufficient conditions under which the risk has the order of the pointwise capped Cramér--Rao bound, and a lower-tail calculation explains the power and logarithmic regimes. We also give conditional guarantees when the cluster center, separation, and source count are unknown, with an additional low-noise requirement for count selection. A calibrated covariance factor model illustrates the same criterion beyond source localization.

title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
abstract: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours. The argument behind these recurrences shows that such a colouring gives $W(r,k)>q(W(r-\lceil r/h\rceil,k)-1)$ for all $r\ge h$. We show that cubic, quartic, quintic and sextic residue colourings give $k$-polychromatic blocks with $q$ much larger than $k$ (e.g. $q=1,376,317$ for $h=3$ and $k=28$), and use them to get explicit lower bounds. For three colours and $9\le k\le28$ we improve on every published bound we know of, among them $W(3,9)>4,002,705$ and $W(3,28)>159,594,201,561,100,726$. For $3\le r\le6$ and $9\le k\le28$, $77$ of the $80$ cases improve on what the published bounds give under these recurrences and the other three tie. For $r=5$ and $12\le k\le15$ the best values come from palettes that are cyclic intervals of colours indexed by quintic residues. We checked every block by exhaustive enumeration and every base colouring by computer. We also prove that the block modulus is at most $(W(2,k)-1)/(k-1)$, so the method does not improve the asymptotics. For large $k$ the largest cubic block modulus lies between $k^{4-\varepsilon}$ and $k^2 4^k$.

title: A Novel Matrix-Free Approximate Elemental Inverse for Efficient Preconditioning of Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Elements
abstract: Efficient matrix-free preconditioning remains a challenge for discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretisations of elliptic problems, particularly for general element shapes with collapsed-coordinate bases, such as prisms, tetrahedra and pyramids. Multigrid provides a promising framework, but its efficiency depends strongly on the effectiveness and computational cost of the smoother. For modal bases, point Jacobi can provide insufficient smoothing, whereas applying block Jacobi through stored dense inverses incurs substantial storage and computational costs. We propose a matrix-free approximate elemental inverse, an approximation to the inverse of each elemental diagonal block, constructed from inverse modal-to-nodal transforms and an element-dependent sparse matrix. Its application exploits generalised sum-factorisation and partial sum-factorisation in collapsed coordinates, avoiding the explicit storage and multiplication of large dense matrices. The method is evaluated as both a standalone preconditioner and a multigrid smoother on hexahedral, prismatic, tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. Although the proposed approximation generally increases iteration counts compared to exact block Jacobi, the cost per iteration is far lower. This trade-off yields substantial reductions in total solution time for hexahedral and prismatic elements, while achieving comparable performance for tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. This study can also serve as a practical guide for tuning the convergence of the discontinuous Galerkin interior-penalty Poisson solver.

title: Closed-form Optimal Solutions for Propulsive-Differential Drag Control of Spacecraft Swarms
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimal control approach for Distributed Space Systems (DSS) to minimize the total delta-v cost for large, time-constrained reconfigurations. Reconfiguration cost is decreased by blending differential drag and propulsive control within the same control window. By parameterizing the problem with Relative Orbital Elements (ROE) and leveraging reachable set theory, a maneuver planning methodology is derived to produce provably-optimal, full roto-translational control solutions in closed-form, such that they can be implemented on hardware-limited spacecraft.

title: Trivial Iwasawa modules and arithmetic linking numbers
abstract: We give a computable criterion of the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa module over the maximal multiple $\mathbb Z_p$-extension of a number filed in which an odd prime number $p$ splits completely. This criterion is obtained from the description of the presentation matrix of the Galois coinvariant of the Iwasawa module by arithmetic linking numbers. The description is based on the Koch type presentation of a pro-$p$ Galois group with restricted ramification, which is analogous to the Milnor presentation of a link group from a viewpoint of arithmetic topology.

title: On perfectoid ideals
abstract: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear algebra algorithm for computing finite approximations of such generators. We illustrate this by an explicit approximation modulo $8$ of an element $σ\in (t-1)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/2^{\infty}}\rangle$ which admits compatible sequences of $2$-power roots and satisfies $σ\equiv t-1\pmod{2}$.

title: Perturbed Exponential Systems, Pattern-Dependent Shifted-Sinc Operators, and Matrix Symbols on Finite Unions of Intervals
abstract:
We study perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted frequency lattices through shifted-sinc operators and finite-dimensional fiberizations. For the auxiliary binary local-shift model, we identify the exact pattern-dependent invariant $$ ρ_{δ,s}=\|P_-T_{2δ}P_+\|, $$ which gives the optimal squared synthesis bounds $1\pmρ_{δ,s}$. For periodic patterns, the synthesis operator reduces exactly to a single constant Vandermonde-type matrix, yielding finite-dimensional basis criteria and optimal bounds. We further prove that the worst binary lower bound is the infimum of its periodic counterparts; at the critical value $δ=1/4$, a step pattern is governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has vanishing lower bound, although every fixed periodic pattern remains invertible.
  We also combine exact bounds for structured patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, obtaining explicit stability neighborhoods. For finite unions of bounded intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, folding modulo one yields finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the exact bounds and complete Riesz-sequence, frame, and Riesz-basis criteria. This framework also yields finite Hadamard constraints for periodic spectra and an exact reduction of rationally commensurate multirate sampling.

title: The Pu inequality and the Viterbo conjecture with finite symmetry
abstract: We study a construction for producing Finsler metrics on the sphere from convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ using the quaternions. Among several applications, we prove the weak Viterbo conjecture for convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are invariant under the natural action of the quaternion group $Q$. This is the first instance where Viterbo's systolic inequality is established for convex bodies with a finite group symmetry, addressing a question of Haim-Kislev-Ostrover. Moreover, a smooth $Q$-symmetric convex domain that achieves equality is symplectomorphic to the ball, without any assumption of strict or uniform convexity. Finally, we show that any link of minimal Reeb orbits on the boundary of a uniformly convex $Q$-symmetric convex body is transversely isotopic to a union of Hopf fibers, strengthening a result of Abbondandolo-Edtmair-Kang in the $Q$-symmetric setting.

title: On Parameterization of Some Problems in Number Theory
abstract: The article is devoted to the parametric solution of some Diophantine equations with two variables. In essence, we find an additional parametric relationship between the solution of the original equation and the simpler linear equation ax - by = 1. The method of hidden parameters helps to obtain a parametric representation of integer solutions for a number of problems in number theory. The method consists in that, first, instead of each quantity included in the original equation, we introduce an additional number of parameters using a linear or non-linear function, which allows us to find both connections between the parameters and some parametric solution of the desired equation. Then we reset (nullify) the introduced linear or non-linear functional dependence (hidden parameters), which in the original formulation of the problem would mean just changing the letter designation of the parameters. However, as a result of these actions, a simplified parametric solution is obtained and the found relationship between the parameters remains. In this paper, the method is discussed in detail using the example of parametric solving such Diophantine equation as the Pell equation. The method of such parameterization is also applied to problems related to Pell's equation. The methods of parameterization are discussed for the Delaunay equation, the Nagell equation and similar equations of higher powers.

title: Linear Stability and a Turning Point Principle for Barotropic Liquid Stars with a Free Boundary in General Relativity
abstract: We study the linear stability of spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat steady states of the Einstein-Euler system describing a liquid star surrounded by vacuum. The equation of state has positive surface density, positive causal sound speed, and an asymptotically linear high-density limit. We construct the equilibrium family and derive the linearized equation with a Robin boundary condition. The linearized operator has discrete real spectrum, and its negative Morse index equals the number of growing modes. We prove that the linearized operator around steady states with large central redshift admits a growing mode, while such growing modes do not exist for steady states with small central redshift. A parameter derivative of the equilibrium family provides a regular interior zero solution of the linearized equation, whose boundary defect is a nonzero multiple of the parameter derivative of the total mass. This gives a turning point principle: the kernel is one-dimensional precisely at mass critical points, and the sign of the crossing eigenvalue is determined by the bending of the mass-radius curve.

title: Divisorial ideals and $v$-class semigroups of strictly closed domains
abstract: We study divisorial ideals and the $v$-class semigroup of a Noetherian domain satisfying Serre's condition $(S_2)$. We prove that strict closedness is equivalent to Clifford $v$-regularity and describe the structure of the associated $v$-class semigroup. We use these results to characterize finite generation of the class semigroup and Boole $v$-regularity. We also construct prime ideal decompositions of integrally closed divisorial ideals and clarify the relationship between these decompositions and local Boole $v$-regularity. Finally, we study polynomial extensions and use them to construct Boole $v$-regular and locally Boole $v$-regular domains in arbitrary dimension.

title: Comparison of Logarithmic Hochschild Homologies
abstract: We construct a comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}$ between Rognes' logarithmic Hochschild homology and Olsson's logarithmic Hochschild homology which generalizes the comparison between Gabber's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Gab}}$ and Olsson's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In particular, Olsson's comparison is recovered as the first associated graded piece of our comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In the development of this comparison, we also prove a descent result for the cotangent complex generalizing a result of Bhatt, and construct a notion of HKR completed Hochschild homology for a general morphism of derived stacks which is functorial in the morphism and generalizes existing constructions of Hochschild homology when the base is affine.

title: Multilevel Monte Carlo for Polytopic DG Discretisations with Spatially Represented Random Coefficients
abstract: We develop a multilevel Monte Carlo framework for coercive elliptic problems with random diffusion and reaction coefficients on polytopic meshes, with particular emphasis on the approximation and inter-level coupling of random coefficients generated from spatially represented latent fields. The main analytical contribution is a Strang-type error decomposition in a DG norm that separates the forward discretisation error from the error introduced by approximating the random coefficients. On this basis, we study two coefficient-generation and multilevel-coupling strategies, a spectral sampler based on a stationary Gaussian latent field defined on a fixed Cartesian reference grid, and an SPDE-based Matérn sampler in which levels are coupled through projected white-noise loads on agglomerated hierarchies. Both fit into the same coefficient-aware analytical framework and couple adjacent levels directly through a common latent random input. The theory is supported by numerical experiments on general Voronoi and agglomerated polytopic meshes, demonstrating the predicted forward and coefficient-representation errors, decay of multilevel corrections, strong inter-level coupling, and the resulting work-accuracy behaviour relative to single-level Monte Carlo.

title: The Calabi-Yau and Sullivan conjectures for minimal surfaces with symmetries
abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a connected open Riemann surface \(X\) by holomorphic automorphisms and acting on a Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge 3\), by orthogonal transformations. In a previous paper, the second author gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a \(G\)-equivariant conformal minimal immersion \(F:X\to\mathbb R^n\), and he asked whether such \(F\) can be chosen to be a proper map. Assuming that this condition holds, we give an affirmative answer when \(X\) is a bordered Riemann surface and \(G\) acts freely on the boundary of \(X\). This contributes to the Sullivan conjecture concerning the existence of proper hyperbolic minimal surfaces in \(\mathbb R^3\) of finite topology. Under the same conditions, we also construct a \(G\)-equivariant proper conformal minimal immersion of \(X\) to the unit ball of \(\mathbb R^n\) which is complete in the induced metric, thereby opening a new direction in the Calabi--Yau theory regarding the study of complete bounded minimal surfaces. Analogous results hold for null curves in \(\mathbb C^n\).

title: Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of symmetric powers and applications
abstract: The Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class $c_{SM}(X)$ is defined in the Chow group $A_*(X)$ of a scheme $X$, and generalizes $c(T_X)\cap [X]$ if $X$ is smooth. In this paper we independently compute $c_{SM}(S^nX)\in A_*(S^nX)$ modulo $n!$ torsion; we use this result to compute the pushforward to $S^nX$ of $c_{SM}(Quot^n_X(E))$ (and in particular $c_{SM}(Hilb^n X)$) when $X$ is smooth and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$. Finally, when $X$ is smooth and complete of dimension $3$ we propose a refined version of the the MNOP conjecture that computes the image of the pushforward of $[Hilb^n X]^{vir}$ to $A_0(S^nX)$ and prove it modulo $n!$ torsion when $X$ is Calabi-Yau.

title: Tate Frobenius and chromatic blueshift of finite spectra
abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $n\geq 1$. We prove that the Tate-Frobenius of the $\operatorname{K}(n)$-local sphere induces an equivalence between $L_{n-1}L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y$ and $(L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y)^{tΣ_p} \cong (L_nY)^{tΣ_p}$ for any finite $p$-local type $n-1$ spectrum $Y$ with trivial $Σ_p$-action.

title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
abstract: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements. Constructing analogs of the higher Bruhat orders in other settings is an area of recent interest, including recent work of Hothem for permutations in $S_{n}$. We give a construction that generalizes any interval $[\mathrm{id},w]$ in the weak order where $w$ is an element of the affine symmetric group $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$. Our construction recovers the classical higher Bruhat orders when $w$ is the longest element in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Paralleling the classical case, we show that the second higher Bruhat order is a ranked poset on commutation classes of reduced words for $w\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$, allowing us to prove a conjecture due to Elias. When $w\in \mathfrak{S}_n$, we also establish results for our higher Bruhat orders that are direct analogs of numerous results in the classical higher Bruhat orders.

title: Stochastic Geometry Meets Optimization: Data-Driven Cellular Planning
abstract: Deployment optimization of base stations (BSs) is critical for improving cellular network performance metrics such as coverage and capacity, impacting user experience, scalability, and infrastructure cost-effectiveness. Traditional methods that optimize precise BS locations do not generally provide broader insights into spatial deployment priorities or alternative viable deployments. Stochastic geometry approaches, on the other hand, offer a more interpretable intensity-based framework, but rarely utilize real-world user location data or investigate optimal BS deployment strategies. In this work, we propose a data-driven stochastic geometry-based approach that optimizes BS deployment intensity to maximize a network performance metric using samples from an unknown user-location distribution. We specialize the framework to an inhomogeneous Poisson point process (PPP) for cellular coverage analysis. The resulting infinite-dimensional problem is discretized over the deployment area and solved using sampled user locations. We characterize the discretization and sampling errors, apply stochastic mirror ascent to solve the empirical problem, and analyze the selection of concrete BS deployments using independent validation samples. Unlike traditional methods, our approach yields an optimized spatial intensity that reveals deployment priorities across regions and accommodates practical deployment constraints, multi-tier networks, and incremental deployment scenarios. Numerical experiments with synthetic and real-world spatial demand data demonstrate the proposed approach under different network configurations.

title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
abstract: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the $L^2$-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the $H^1$-norm.

title: Ozone groups and centers of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras
abstract: Let $p,q$ be roots of unity with $pq\neq1$, and put $\ell=|\langle p,q\rangle|$ and $t=\ord(pq)$. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is $μ_\ell\timesμ_{\ell/t}$, generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order $t$. We give a presentation of the center as a hypersurface over a cyclic quotient surface singularity. It is regular exactly when $1$ is a characteristic root, which disproves a conjecture of Chan, Gaddis, Won and Zhang, and Gorenstein exactly when $p^{m/h}=q^{n/h}$, where $m=\ord(p)$, $n=\ord(q)$ and $h=\gcd(m,n)$; for $p=ζ_5$, $q=ζ_5^{2}$ it is not. We also decide when the fixed ring of the ozone group is Gorenstein and when $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ is Calabi--Yau, and show that the algebras with regular center have non-affine automorphisms and nonzero locally nilpotent derivations.

title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods
abstract: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones. Along the way, we describe the dual variety of $X$ in terms of the Whittaker cotangent bundle and regular centralizers, viewed as Coulomb branches.

title: Timed Recovery Safe Gradient Flows for Constrained Nonlinear Programming
abstract: This paper studies how to relax pointwise feasibility in continuous-time dynamics for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming while retaining a quantitative feasible-recovery guarantee. Existing safe gradient flows enforce forward invariance of the feasible set, which yields an anytime-feasible dynamics but can be overly restrictive for optimization because it suppresses transient infeasible motion that may be essential for effective descent. To address this limitation, we propose a timed recovery safe gradient flow that replaces pointwise feasibility with fixed-horizon feasible recovery. The proposed construction augments the state with a timer that records the elapsed infeasible duration and computes a minimum-norm correction to the nominal gradient flow through a pointwise convex quadratic program. We show that the resulting augmented safe set is forward invariant and that every trajectory initialized from the feasible set returns to it within every time window of length \(τ\). We further show that, in a strict interior inactive regime, the closed-loop dynamics reduces exactly to the nominal gradient flow and recovers the corresponding local convergence behavior. Numerical examples illustrate how the recovery horizon shapes the closed-loop behavior and corroborate the theoretical analysis.

title: The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers
abstract:
Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colonΔ_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^α$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[
  \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{α+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}. \]

title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global Hölder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally Hölder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global Hölder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.

title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.

title: Equifacetted polytopes whose facets are products of simplices: The simplicial prism case
abstract: We study \emph{prismatical} polytopes, those all of whose facets are combinatorially isomorphic to the simplicial prism $Δ^{d-2}\timesΔ^1$. In dimension three these are exactly the cubical polytopes, so the class sits naturally between simplicial and cubical polytopes. In dimension four, $Δ^2\timesΔ^2$ is the simplest prismatical polytope and we can construct infinitely many by using connected sums. By fibreing a triangle over a triangulated polygon we construct infinitely many connected-sum-prime prismatical $4$-polytopes. Finally, we show that there are no prismatical $d$-polytopes for $d\ge5$, answering a question of Perles and Shephard.

title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
abstract:
For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy.
  The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.

title: Spectrum of the basilica group and the associated real and complex 2D dynamics
abstract: In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar. Finally, this yields some consequences on the properties of the density of states measures and its support.

title: A frame-indifferent rank-one convex function in three dimensions which is not quasiconvex
abstract: We construct a function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}\to\mathbb{R}$ which is frame-indifferent, $W(QF)=W(F)$ for all $Q\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$, rank-one convex, but not quasiconvex. In a neighbourhood of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ the function is an explicit polynomial of degree four in the strain $F^TF-\mathrm{Id}$; the failure of quasiconvexity occurs at $F=\mathrm{Id}$ through a third-order mechanism of Šverák type, with test functions whose gradients are arbitrarily close to $\mathrm{Id}$. The polynomial is obtained from a geometrically linear example, a rank-one convex, non-quasiconvex quartic polynomial of the symmetric part of the gradient, by evaluating it at the strain $\frac12(F^TF-\mathrm{Id})$, adding a uniaxial prestress and a cubic correction, and enlarging the quartic term. The local function is extended to all of $\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}$ by adding a frame-indifferent polyconvex function which vanishes near $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. This work was carried out with the assistance of the AI model Claude Opus 5.5; the proofs of the main results have been formally verified in Lean 4.

title: Weak adversarial tensor neural network for high-dimensional Fokker-Planck equations
abstract: Solving high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck (SFP) equations remains challenging. Recently, deep learning methods have shown great potential for solving high-dimensional SFP equations due to their universal approximation and mesh-free training. However, the high-dimensional integrals involved in loss computation and normalization can be expensive to approximate accurately using Monte Carlo integration. To address this issue, we propose a weak adversarial tensor neural network (WATNN) method for solving high-dimensional SFP equations, which combines a weak adversarial (WA) formulation with the tensor neural network (TNN). The WA formulation avoids the cross terms introduced by squaring the strong residual, reducing the number of integrals to be computed. When both the primal network and the adversarial test network are set as TNNs, the TNN quadrature scheme provides accurate and efficient normalization and loss computation with relatively few fixed quadrature points, avoiding the statistical sampling error that arises when using Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the effectiveness numerically on four high-dimensional SFP equations. For the 6D unimodal, 6D multi-modal, 10D multi-modal and 20D multi-modal problems, WATNN achieves the mean relative errors of 1.50%, 1.13%, 1.20% and 7.93% respectively, in only a few minutes.

title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^α$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $α\in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $α= 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $α= 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $α$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.

title: The permutation and automorphism groups of univariate multiplicity codes
abstract: We give explicit characterizations of the permutations and linear isometries that leave (univariate) multiplicity codes invariant. We consider any evaluation subset of the finite field, any multiplicity and dimension, and the automorphisms are with respect to the Niederreiter-Rosenblom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric. For multiplicity one, we recover the permutation and automorphism groups of classical Reed--Solomon codes in the classical Hamming metric. In the main dimension range, automorphisms are uniquely determined by a projectivity that permutes the evaluation subset, up to multiplication by a nonzero scalar. For multiplicity one, permutations are given by affine maps that permute the evaluation subset. In contrast, for multiplicity at least two, permutations are only given by translations that permute the evaluation subset. Finally, we give an algebraic characterization of automorphisms of multiplicity codes for the folded Hamming metric.

title: Quantitative nodal domain count for Maass forms
abstract: We consider a real even Hecke-Maass cusp form $φ$ on the modular surface, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. We prove that its restriction to any fixed compact segment $β$ of the vertical geodesic above $i$ has $\gg_{β,\varepsilon} T^{1/6-\varepsilon}$ sign changes, yielding the same lower bound for the number of distinct inert nodal domains meeting the segment. Building on ideas of Jang-Jung and Jung-Young, we study correlations between values at points on the vertical geodesic separated by distances of order $T^{-1}$. Using arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity and Dirichlet-polynomial estimates, we show that the correlation is negative for a suitable choice of separation. An elementary counting argument and the Iwaniec-Sarnak supremum bound then give the claimed lower bound.

title: Divisor Sums with Spacing Constraints
abstract: For $x,y>0$ let $S(x,y)$ denote the largest value of $\sum_{n\in A}τ(n)$ over subsets $A$ of $[1,x]\cap\N$ whose elements are pairwise separated by more than $y$ (here $τ$ is the divisor function). We determine the order of magnitude, and in a subrange the precise asymptotic, of $S(x,y)$ when the spacing parameter $y$ ranges over a polylogarithmic scale $y=(\log x)^{1+λ(\logλ-1)}$, $λ>1$. We show that for every fixed $λ>2$ the spacing constraint costs a computable power of $\log x$ in the exponent, while for every fixed $1<λ<2$ it costs nothing at all: $S(x,y)\sim x\log x$, the same asymptotic as the unconstrained sum $\sum_{n\le x}τ(n)$. Near the threshold $λ=2$ the two regimes meet, and we show that for any fixed $κ>0,$ $S(x,y)\asymp_κ x\log x$ uniformly as long as $λ\le 2+2κ/\sqrt{\log\log x}$. The proof combines the Sathe-Selberg distribution of the number of prime factors, a smooth squarefree estimate obtained from a generating function together with Cauchy's formula, a sieve estimate for correlations among the squarefree parts of the integers that contribute most heavily to $\sum_{n\le x}τ(n)$, and two combinatorial devices (the Caro-Wei bound and a concentration inequality on the symmetric group) used to extract a well-spaced independent set from a sparse auxiliary graph.

title: Sphere decomposition for finite subgroups of 3-manifold mapping class groups
abstract: For a closed, oriented 3-manifold $M$, we show that any finite subgroup of its mapping class group preserves an isotopy class of filling sphere system on $M$. This is an isotopy version of the "equivariant sphere theorem" of Meeks-Yau. As part of our analysis, we establish a bijection between simplices of the Guirardel--Levitt outer space for $π_1(M)$ and filling sphere systems in $M$, generalizing an argument of Hatcher. We also compute the image of $\mathrm{Homeo}(M)\to\mathrm{Out}(π_1M)$ for any such $M$.

title: Graph distance and percolation dimension of three-dimensional Brownian motion
abstract: We prove that the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a continuous curve joining $W_0$ to $W_1$ within the range $W([0,1])$ of a three-dimensional Brownian motion is almost surely a deterministic constant $γ_3\in(1,5/3]$. Moreover, we construct continuum many simple curves with pairwise distinct images that attain this minimum. Each curve has box dimension $γ_3$ and admits a parametrization that is $β$-Hölder for every $0<β<1/γ_3$. To identify $γ_3$, we partition Brownian time into $n$ equal intervals and form a graph by joining pairs with intersecting ranges. We show that its endpoint graph distance and diameter have a common deterministic almost sure growth exponent $θ$ and that $γ_3=2θ$. We also establish $n^{pθ+o(1)}$ growth for their $p$-th moments, for every $p>0$.

title: Continuous-Time Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Control: Limits, Duality, and Stability
abstract: A sampled robust control problem averages future values over disturbance laws, while its continuous-time counterpart evolves with an averaged drift. We establish a fluid limit connecting these two models for Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Under a uniform disturbance moment bound and subcritical growth, sampled Bellman values converge locally uniformly to the upper and lower values of a discounted differential game. The argument accommodates unbounded disturbances without requiring square-integrable increments. We also derive an explicit bound on the change in either game value when both the radius and center of the ambiguity set vary. For Euclidean disturbance space, uniform Lipschitz continuity in the disturbance, common state and cost Lipschitz bounds, and a discount rate exceeding the drift's state Lipschitz constant, this estimate converts distributional confidence bounds into uniform value approximation bounds. Static Wasserstein duality reformulates pointwise distributional optimization; affine disturbance dependence permits an exact reduction to a ball of means. Experiments illustrate the common limit and decreasing value error with sample size. For a nonlinear disturbance model, uniform shifts overestimate worst-case recovery speed by about 36\%. In a two-product inventory model, increasing ambiguity raises production near balance while reducing the region of full production in deeper backlogs.

title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $μ=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^μ, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $μ$.

title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
abstract: Let $(X, Ω)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $Ω$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, Ω)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau. We further give a valuative criterion detecting K-semistability of the degeneration by a negative valuation.

title: Strengthening AC optimal power flow relaxation through offline bound tightening and linear approximations
abstract: The alternating-current optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem is fundamental to power system operation and planning, but its nonconvexity makes globally optimal solutions of large-scale instances computationally challenging. Convex relaxations provide tractable lower bounds for assessing solution quality and supporting global optimization, although their effectiveness depends strongly on relaxation strength. This paper proposes an offline convexification and bound tightening framework for constructing strong linear programming (LP) relaxations for families of related ACOPF instances. Rather than repeating the tightening procedure for each instance, we compute variable bounds and second-order cone outer-approximation (SOC-OA) cuts offline using a demand-slack model and reuse them for subsequent instances with the same topology and admissible demand variations. Computational results on PGLib instances show that the fully offline approach achieves an average gap of $4.32\%$, compared with $3.80\%$ for the fully online approach, while achieving an average speedup of approximately $272\times$. The results demonstrate that offline convexification and bound tightening can recover most of the relaxation improvement of online tightening while significantly reducing the computational burden for repeated ACOPF evaluations.

title: Kashiwara's Lemma for Potent D-modules
abstract: On stacks there is a richer version of $\mathcal{D}$-modules---called $\textit{potent }\mathcal{D}\textit{-modules}$---which decompletes at equivariant parameters, in the same sense that genuine equivariant $K$-theory decompletes equivariant cohomology. In this paper, we prove a ``genuine'' version of Kashiwara's lemma for $\mathcal{D}$-modules. Namely, we show that for a broad class of geometric stacks $X$, if $Z \subset X$ is a closed substack, the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $Z$ is equivalent under pushforward to the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}} _Z(X)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $X$ with support contained in $Z$.

title: Closed-form Optimal Propulsive-Differential Drag Control for Large Reconfigurations of Spacecraft Swarms
