Conversely, nilpotent $2$-representations on such categories yield affine Brauer actions with spectrum contained in $\mathbb Z$. At the fixed vertex $0$, we directly define corrected generators and verify the nil-Brauer and mixed relations. For $\mathbf u$-admissible integral parameters at arbitrary positive level, we prove an isomorphism between the locally unital algebras of the cyclotomic Brauer category and a cyclotomic quotient of the principal $2$-representation. This gives compatible $\mathbb Z$-gradings on the category and its endomorphism algebras, providing a Brauer analogue of the graded realization of type $A$ cyclotomic Hecke algebras. Over algebraically closed fields of odd characteristic $p$, we also obtain both constructions with spectrum contained in $\mathbb F_p$, for the mixed affine datum restricted to its spectral weight subgroup.

title: Distortion-Rate Outage Probability for Non-ergodic Classes of Sources
abstract: The concept of outage has been commonly used in the context of transmission rates over non-ergodic channels. For those channels, one channel state or realization may be encountered for the whole transmission duration of a codeword. In the dual setting of source coding and whenever source statistics are not ergodic, we define in this work the notion of outage; we discuss related properties, consider the special case of compact source classes and provide examples.

title: Finite stabilization, socle extensions, and Faith's conjecture
abstract: We give a length-two counterexample to the unrestricted product comparison in Bergman's Question 3.1, positive criteria for quasi-injective common modules, and a semidirect-product version of Question 3.2. For semiprimary right self-injective rings, the countable hull construction yields a cyclic two-layer witness, its Baer class, and an opposite-side extension obstruction. We apply this construction over the square-zero ring of the counterexample. The hull quotient of a countable sum of injectives is the endomorphism space modulo finite-rank maps, and computes the full socle-radical defect of a countable product of the regular module. This gives a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors. The original length-two product embeds its defect in the same quotient through an explicit intersection, and all associated extension classes arise from one specified Baer class. The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.

title: StarRTT: An End-to-End Real-Time Framework for Blind Zone-Free RTT Prediction in Starlink LEO Satellite Networks
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations such as Starlink require frequent handovers due to high orbital velocities, resulting in substantial Round-Trip Time (RTT) fluctuations. Accurate RTT prediction can mitigate these fluctuations, yet it fundamentally relies on continuously updated serving- satellite information. Existing serving-satellite identification methods typically complete identification only at the end of each scheduling cycle, creating an identification blind zone that limits real-time prediction. To overcome this limitation, we develop StarRTT, an end-to-end real-time framework that eliminates the blind zone by integrating per-second serving-satellite identification with RTT prediction. Within this framework, we propose Real-Time Long Short-Term Memory (RT-LSTM), an LSTM-based RTT prediction model designed to capture both non-stationary RTT evolution and time-varying geometric relationships among the serving satellite, user terminal, and gateways. Specifically, a historical LSTM encodes historical RTT observations and real-time serving-satellite and gateway-relative features, while a future LSTM processes Two-Line Element (TLE)-propagated future features of the identified serving satellite up to the next scheduling instant. Under strict real-time back-testing, RT-LSTM achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.405 ms averaged over all 15 prediction horizons and 15 reference time-slot indices, reducing the error by 4.3 %, 11.6 %, and 22.1 % compared with the existing baseline models, LSTM, StarNet, and Attention-based Spatiotemporal Model (ASTM), respectively. Notably, the reduction over LSTM reaches 12.5 % at the scheduling instant, highlighting the benefit of real-time serving-satellite information when recent RTT observations are limited.

title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

title: Joint q-Numerical Ranges of Continuous Operator-Valued Functions
abstract: This paper develops a unified theory of joint $q$-numerical ranges $\Fq(F)$ for continuous functions $F:\Om \to \B(\cH)$, where $\Om$ is a compact Hausdorff space and $\B(\cH)$ denotes the $C^*$-algebra of bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $\cH$. We prove that $\Fq(F)$ is totally bounded in $\cC(\Om)$, the space of continuous complex-valued functions on $\Om$, and establish the upper semicontinuity of the set-valued map $F\mapsto \Fq(F)$, and show that $\Fq(F)$ is compact when $\cH$ is finite-dimensional. The main result of the paper is a realization theorem. We prove that, for every totally bounded subset $K$ of $\cC(\Om)$ and every $q\in \C$ with $|q|=1$, there exist a Hilbert space $\cH$ and a continuous function $F:\Om\to\B(\cH)$ such that $qK\subset \Fq(F)\subset q\cok$. Consequently, if $K$ is closed and convex, then $\Fq(F)=qK$. As applications, we derive analogous realization results for bounded subsets in $\C^n$ and for totally bounded subsets in arbitrary Banach spaces.

title: Marked length spectrum and area of surfaces with Anosov geodesic flow
abstract: More than twenty years ago, Croke and Dairbekov showed that a negatively curved metric $g_0$ on a closed surface has minimal area among all negatively curved Riemannian metrics $g$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $g_0$. We show that the curvature assumption on the second metric can be removed and extend this result to reversible Finsler metrics. More precisely, we prove that a reversible Finsler metric $F_0$ on a closed surface whose geodesic flow is Anosov has minimal area among all reversible Finsler metrics $F$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $F_0$.

title: Schur--Weyl duality for coideal subalgebras of quantum affine superalgebras of type $A$
abstract: We extend the results of \cite{FLLLWW20} to the super setting. More precisely, we define two families of coideal sub-superalgebras of quantum affine superalgebras of type $A$, called $\jmath$- and $\imath$-quantum affine superalgebras respectively, and establish Schur--Weyl duality between them and affine Hecke algebras of type $C$.

title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we prove that an annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.

title: On the closure under barycenters of location-scatter families with a normalized generator
abstract: We provide an example of a normalized absolutely continuous probability whose location-scatter family (LSF) does not contain all the 2-Wassertein geodesics passing through its elements. In particular, we find a counterexample for Corollary 4.5 in [2]. Finally, we prove that LSFs with a (possibly singular) radially symmetric generator are closed under 2-Wasserstein barycenters.

title: Energies with values in networks and geometric quasiconvexity
abstract:
We study the asymptotic behaviour, as $\varepsilon	o 0^+$, of the $p$-Dirichlet energy of maps $u\colonΩ\subset\mathbb{R}^2 	o \mathbb{R}^2$ constrained to take values in the rescaled periodic network $\varepsilon\mathcal Z$, where $\mathcal Z$ is a standard square network in $\mathbb{R}^2$. The oscillations are carried by the constraint in the target, not by the energy density, and their effect depends on $p$. For $1<p<2$ the constraint disappears in the limit: the $Γ$-limit is an integral functional on the whole of $m{W}^{1,p}(Ω, \mathbb{R}^2 )$, whose density is given by an asymptotic cell formula on tilted cells. This density is equal to $(|a_1|+|a_2|)^p$ on rank-one matrices $a\otimesν$, $|ν|=1$, and exceeds its convex envelope by a quantity comparable to $|\det A|\,|A|^{p-2}$, with constants of order $(2-p)^{-1}$. Consequently, although the original energy density is convex, the limit density is quasiconvex but neither convex nor polyconvex: quasiconvexity is generated by the geometry of the constraint. For $p\ge2$ the constraint survives in the limit as $\det
abla u=0$, and the $Γ$-limit is the degenerate energy $\int_Ω(|
abla u_1|+|
abla u_2|)^p\, m{d} x$, that is, the $p$-energy of $u$ considered as a map into the normed plane $(\mathbb{R}^2,|\cdot|_1)$, the metric limit of the networks.

title: On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs
abstract: Stochastic Push-Pull achieves linear speedup with respect to the network size $n$ on static strongly connected digraphs, but whether this speedup persists on time-varying networks remains unclear. In this work, we construct a quadratic decentralized problem on period-two networks showing that stochastic Push-Pull may fail to attain linear speedup over time-varying digraphs. For $p$-periodic networks, we identify an effective node count $n_{\mathrm{eff}}\le n$ that governs the leading stochastic term. Specifically, for smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence upper bounds and matching lower bounds for stochastic Push-Pull with constant stepsizes, both exhibiting the leading-order dependence $Θ(1/\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{eff}} T})$. When $p=1$, the identity $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=n$ recovers the usual linear speedup for static digraphs. However, periodic networks can have $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=o(n)$, demonstrating the loss of linear speedup under temporal variation. Numerical experiments illustrate effective-count scaling and the separation between static and periodic networks, consistent with our theoretical findings.

title: An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
abstract: In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $χ(S^n_{R}) \leq (ξ_R + o(1))^n$, where $ξ_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-1/(4R^2)) $ and $χ(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.

title: The chromatic number of $\{\mathrm{ISK}_4, \textup{diamond}\}$-free graphs
abstract: An $\mathrm{ISK}_4$ is a graph that is isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$; a \textit{diamond} is $K_4$ minus one edge; and a \textit{bowtie} consists of two triangles sharing exactly one vertex. Lévêque, Maffray, and Trotignon~(2012) conjectured that every $\mathrm{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable. Chen, Chen, Cui, Feng, and Liu~(2021) proved this for $\{\textup{diamond},\textup{bowtie}\}$-free graphs. We prove this conjecture for diamond-free graphs. Moreover, the bound is optimal.

title: MIACE and Monotone Tracking: Exact Tuning for First-Order Plants and Positive Cascades with Pure Delay
abstract: The Module of Integral Absolute Complex Error (MIACE) was created by me 23 years ago. It gave very nice behaviour to the transient response of the controlled systems I tested. It combines absolute tracking-error and equilibrium-centered command areas. For a stable unit-gain plant with known pure delay, an exact identity separates squared MIACE excess into a negative-area penalty and a weighted area imbalance. The resulting lower bound depends on the plant's first low-frequency moment and the delay. Every attaining response of a positive cascade is monotone, independently of controller structure. For a first-order plant, output variation and peak overshoot also admit quantitative bounds. Exact conditions identify the unique positive PI controller attaining the delayed bound; filtered PID extends attainment beyond this PI range. For cascades of arbitrary order, Hermite interpolation and a finite-support delay remainder construct proper rational controllers of the same order, with internal exponential stability proved by positive convolution representations. An exponential-moment characterization then closes the attainment question when internal delay blocks are allowed: an ordinary command attains the bound if and only if $α>μ+δ-1$. An explicit internal-model controller realizes every feasible weight and delay. A sharp amplitude-cap condition determines the least command peak among all attaining responses and the complete capped sign-preserving area front. A small-gain estimate supplies an explicit MIACE deviation bound under delay error. A storage balance also extends the exact MIACE identity and monotone attainment to a nonlinear first-order class without delay. Independent physical integrations retain delays exactly; quadratic comparisons provide complementary benchmarks.

title: The Malt'sev condition for groups is not categorical
abstract: In this paper we prove that the Mal'tsev condition expressing the existence of group operations is not equivalent to a categorical property. More precisely, using pseudo-invertible idempotents, we construct two varieties $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}(f)$ which are equivalent as categories, and such that $\mathcal{V}$ admits group operations, whereas $\mathcal{V}(f)$ does not. We also show that those Mal'tsev conditions which are equivalent to a categorical property have a trivial spectrum.

title: Peaking self-similar solutions and continuation after blow-up for a quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation
abstract: We consider the quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation $$ u_t=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,T), $$ in the range of exponents and dimension $$ N\geq3, \quad σ\in(-2,\infty), \quad m>1, \quad p>p_S(σ)=\frac{m(N+2σ+2)}{N-2}. $$ We establish sharp ranges of exponents $(m,p,σ)$ guaranteeing existence of \emph{peaking solutions} in backward self-similar form $$ u(x,t)=(T-t)^{-α}f(|x|(T-t)^{-β}). $$ By peaking solutions we understand solutions blowing up at a finite time $T\in(0,\infty)$ but allowing for a continuation after the blow-up time. As a remarkable outcome, a number of ranges of exponents $σ$ and $m$ for which peaking solutions exist for any $p>p_S(σ)$ are deduced, contrasting to the previously considered exponent $σ=0$, where a Lepin-type critical exponent $p_L$ provides an upper bound for $p$.

title: Geometry property of stochastic parabolic equations and Prékopa-Leindler inequality on bounded domains
abstract: We study the preservation of spatial concavity and log-concavity for stochastic parabolic equations posed on bounded convex domains. For the linear noise, by using Minkowski convolutions, we establish the convexity preservation of solution almost surely. For the nonlinear noise, by using Itô formula, the impact of noise is given. Moreover, we establish the relationship between the weighted (stochastic) Prékopa-Leindler inequality and properties of (stochastic) parabolic equation on bounded domain, which is new even for deterministic case.

title: Nadler Theorem on Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
abstract: We introduce a generalized metric space endowed with a weighted graph and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points for set-valued mappings that satisfy a contractive condition only along the links of the graph. To demonstrate the applicability and significance of our results, several illustrative examples are presented. As an application, we establish the solvability of a class of integral problems involving set-valued data.

title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
abstract: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.

title: Wasserstein bounds for invariant measures in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation with stable noise
abstract: We study invariant position distributions in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation for Langevin equations driven by rotationally symmetric \(α\)-stable noise, with \(α\in(1,2)\). Under global Lipschitz continuity and dissipativity of the drift, we establish a Wasserstein-1 bound of order \(m^{1/α}\) between the invariant position distribution of the underdamped system and the invariant distribution of its overdamped limit, where $m>0$ is the mass parameter. The proof combines a corrected-position test function with a regularized Stein equation. Cancellation of the transport and friction terms reduces the comparison to a first-moment estimate for the stationary velocity.

title: Coefficient duality and interpolation of Euclidean flag Besov spaces
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to develop the duality theory of the homogeneous Besov spaces associated with the Euclidean flag, using the discrete Littlewood--Paley--Stein analysis. We first establish an exact discrete sampling formula together with bounded analysis and synthesis maps, by which the space is identified with a sequence space of coefficients. The continuous dual is then computed through a coefficient norm. In this computation the geometry of the sampling rectangles plays an essential role: when the spatial exponent is below one, the volume of a dyadic rectangle forces an explicit shift of both smoothness indices. We devote particular attention to the supremum sequence exponent. At that endpoint the closure of the flag test functions is characterized by vanishing scale tails, and the limiting tail is comparable to the distance to this closure; every continuous functional on the full space decomposes into a canonical regular part and a part that annihilates the closure, and the latter may be nonzero. For finite exponents the dual is again a flag Besov space. As applications, finite Calderón sums give a quantitative approximation theorem, and the common analysis and synthesis framework yields real and complex interpolation as well as the lifting property. The arguments are based on the exact sampling formula, scalar maximal estimates and the transpose of one bounded coefficient projection.

title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid $3.12.12$, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid $4.8.8$, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid $3.6.3.6$, the elongated triangular grid $3^3.4^2$ and the snub hexagonal grid $3^4.6$. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid $4.6.12$, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid $3.4.6.4$, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid $3^2.4.3.4$.

title: Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz operators, and Conjugations
abstract: In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,λ}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.

title: A New Characterisation of Selflessness
abstract: We characterise the existence of expectation-preserving embeddings of reduced amalgamated free product $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras into norm ultrapowers of the first factor, fixing its diagonal copy pointwise, in terms of complementary compression relations on Hilbert space ultrapowers. This yields new characterisations of Robert's notion of selflessness, selfless inclusions, and relative selflessness with respect to conditional expectations. We also characterise Ozawa's notion of complete selflessness, including its extension to inclusions. We then illustrate the usefulness of these characterisations by establishing complete selflessness for suitable reduced (amalgamated) free products, free Araki--Woods $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, certain Hecke $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, and $q$-Gaussian $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras. Finally, we obtain dynamical characterisations of (complete) $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-selflessness of discrete groups and establish relative selflessness for suitable reduced crossed products.

title: An energy-stable parametric finite element framework for surface diffusion with moving contact lines on curved substrates
abstract: We develop energy-stable parametric finite element methods for surface diffusion of solid films with moving contact lines on curved substrates. Discretizing both the film surface and the substrate patches allows the introduction of linear schemes that are unconditionally energy stable. A nonlinear variant of the schemes ensures that, in addition, the vertices of the substrate approximations remain attached to the true substrate throughout. Moreover, our framework can incorporate anisotropic surface energy densities, for both the film surface and the substrate, as well as different tangential motions. Numerical experiments in two and three space dimensions illustrate the practicality of the introduced methods.

title: Universal neural network approximation of symmetric polyconvex energies and envelopes
abstract: Symmetric polyconvexity provides a sufficient condition for weak lower semicontinuity in small-strain elasticity and a tractable lower bound for the relaxation of non-(quasi)convex energies. Since classical algorithms for computing such functions can be computationally expensive, neural network approximations have recently emerged as an alternative. A central difficulty with establishing such neural network based approaches for symmetric polyconvexity is the additional monotonicity property. As we show, the corresponding weight restrictions on ReLU-based input-convex networks do not yield universal approximation of the lifted representers. Here, we introduce symmetric polyconvex neural networks (SPCNNs) for constitutive modeling and approximation of symmetric polyconvex envelopes. The deep architecture combines convexity with the monotonicity required of a representer in the space of minors. We prove a universal approximation theorem for symmetric polyconvex energies, without requiring isotropy, and quantify the number of affine pieces attainable by the lifted network and derive reduced architectures for isotropic energies. Numerical examples illustrate stress-based regression and approximation of the symmetric polyconvex envelope of a double-well potential. Symmetric polyconvexity is guaranteed by construction, while the accuracy of the fitted energies and envelopes is assessed numerically.

title: Deformations of cohomology classes and spectral sequences
abstract: We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre. This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria. We give various applications to $\mathrm{Ext}$ spectral sequences for complex Lagrangians and the formality results of Melani-Rubió amongst others. For double complexes, we revisit the Khovanov-Qi decomposition on the Rees side and introduce a two-parameter Rees construction over the affine plane. The higher differentials of the two associated spectral sequences correspond to torsion modules supported on the thickened coordinate axes. We obtain degeneration criteria in terms of these modules and an intrinsic characterisation of the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma.

title: New approaches to the Erdős Distinct Subset Sums Problem
abstract: We present a new method of reproving the best known lower bound of the Erdős distinct subset sums problem. Although our lower bound is asymptotically the same as in Dubroff, Fox and Xu, it is slightly better for the case when \(n\) is odd. Besides, we also provide a new lower bound on the second largest element \(a_{n-1}\).

title: On Trace Averages and Sharp Asymptotics for Powers of Haar-Unitary Matrices
abstract: For a Haar-distributed matrix $U \in U(N)$, Rains's power-map theorem represents the spectrum of $U^m$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as a superposition of independent lower-dimensional CUE spectra. We determine how this exact decomposition appears in trace moments and in sharp Gaussian and Poisson limit laws. For averages of mixed trace products, a Charlier--Ewens convolution separates the stable Wick term from its full finite-$N$ correction. A Fredholm factorisation gives sharp total-variation asymptotics for the normalised trace in four regimes, from fixed powers to $m\geq N$. For a fixed trace power $p$, coherent summation of the leading Laguerre correction yields the exact factor $e^{2/p}$. At the mean-spacing scale, we obtain a sharp Poisson limit for the unfolded spectrum of $U^m$ on a fixed interval as $N, m \rightarrow \infty$; its first-order correction, obtained via the second Charlier polynomial, quantifies the residual under-dispersion of local eigenvalue counts.

title: Local rigidity for the sharp Nash inequality
abstract: Let $V$ be a nonempty relatively compact open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ without boundary. We prove that $C_{\mathrm N}(V,g)\ge C_{\mathrm N}(\mathbb R^n)$ and $\int_V \mathrm{Sc}_g dμ_g\ge0$ imply $\mathrm{Rm}_g=0$ on $V$, where $C_{\mathrm N}$ denotes the optimal constant in the Nash inequality and $\mathrm{Sc}_g$ denotes the scalar curvature. This improves an earlier rigidity result of Druet, Hebey, and Vaugon [Int. Math. Res. Not. (1999), no. 14, 735--779].

title: On the complexity of Medvedev reducibility
abstract: The Medvedev lattice is a tool used to classify the complexity of effective closed sets. In this article, we are interested in the complexity of using this tool. In particular, we study the complexity of deciding whether two effective closed sets have the same degree, when one is fixed and the other is given as input. This problem is naturally~$Σ^0_3$, and among other results, we show that for all degrees except the maximal one, the problem reaches its maximal complexity. It turns out that the argument is not uniform and depends on the self-similarity of the fixed degree, a notion that we introduce in this article. The complexity of having maximal degree is particularly difficult to establish, but we obtain a lower bound that almost matches the upper bound. We also show that deciding whether an effective closed set has a degree incomparable with a fixed degree $d$ is $Π^0_3$-complete whenever $\mathbf{0}_s <_s d <_s \mathbf{1}_s$.

title: Characterization of intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type
abstract: We characterize metric measure spaces that satisfy intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type. The considered parabolic Harnack inequalities are intrinsic in the sense that the waiting time depends on the solution. Our main results shows that in a metric measure space with a doubling measure, such an intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequality holds if and only if a Poincaré inequality holds. We thus show that estimates in scale and function dependent intrinsic geometries can characterize scale and location invariant functional inequalities.

title: Exact bounded cohomology of measure-preserving homeomorphism groups of nonorientable hyperbolic manifolds
abstract: Let $M$ be a closed, connected, non-orientable hyperbolic manifold, and let $μ$ be a good measure on $M$. Denote by $Homeo_0(M,μ)$ the identity component of the group of $μ$-preserving homeomorphisms. For every $d\geq2$, we prove that $\dim\overline{EH}_b^d\bigl(Homeo_0(M,μ)\bigr)=\infty$, where $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denotes reduced exact bounded cohomology in degree $d$.

title: An Arbitrary-Order Augmented Lagrangian Discrete De Rham Scheme for Contact Mechanics with Tresca Friction
abstract: We design and analyse an arbitrary-order augmented Lagrangian Discrete de Rham polytopal scheme for contact mechanics in fractured media. The fractures are represented as objects of codimension one in the matrix, a linear elastic medium, and a Tresca friction model is adopted when contact between fracture walls occurs. Both the normal Signorini-type/traction constraint and the Tresca friction law are recast as projection identities, and are combined into a single augmented Lagrangian bilinear form. The displacement is discretised by a DDR space of arbitrary polynomial degree $k\ge 0,$ enriched on the fracture faces by bubble degrees of freedom that ensure stability via the existence of a discrete lifting between the Lagrange multiplier space and the discrete jump of the displacement along the fracture. We establish an abstract error estimate yielding optimal order convergence for the displacement and the Lagrange multiplier variables. Extensive numerical experiments confirm the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the practical accuracy and robustness of the scheme.

title: On the homeomorphism group of the Cantor set: monotone and measure preserving maps
abstract: Let $E$ be the Cantor set, $G=\operatorname{Homeo}(E)$, let $P\le G$ be the group of order preserving homeomorphisms and $L\le G$ the group of homeomorphisms preserving the Cantor--Lebesgue measure $λ$. We study how $G$ is built from these two subgroups. In 2003, Glasner and Weiss stated that $G=LP=PL$. We show that this is not the case, in fact $PL$ and $LP$ are two different proper subsets of $G$. On the other hand, $PL$ is a dense $G_δ$ subset of $G$, the multiplication map $P\times L\to PL$ is a homeomorphism, and $G=PLP=LPL$. In particular, every homeomorphism of $E$ is conjugate to an element of $PL$. We classify the double cosets $PgL$ using special clopen values set. There are continuum many of them, and $PL$ is the only one which is not meager. We prove that $G$ is topologically generated by one element of $P$ and one element of $L$ and these two generators produce the Thompson's group $V$. We also show that the generic homeomorphism of $E$ is the product of a generic element of $P$ and a generic element of $L$. The equality $G=PL$ fails also if $λ$ is replaced by any other full nonatomic measure.

title: Fuglede's theorem in the Heisenberg group
abstract: We prove a Fuglede-type quantitative isoperimetric inequality for the Pansu sphere, the conjectured isoperimetric set in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^1$. We show that, among suitable volume-preserving normal perturbations of the Pansu sphere that are small in a weighted $C^2$-norm, the difference between the sub-Riemannian perimeters of the perturbed and unperturbed regions is bounded below by a positive constant times the square of their $L^1$-distance. The proof is based on a Riemannian approximation argument with uniform estimates.

title: Long-time stability and convergence of a BDF3 method for a parabolic equation with fading memory
abstract: We analyze the long-time stability and convergence of a third-order backward differentiation formula (BDF3) for parabolic equations with exponentially fading memory. The BDF3 scalar resolvent has oscillatory coefficients, so the monotonicity argument used for lower-order formulas in [Math. Comp. 62 (1994) 477-496] does not apply. We instead control memory feedback by the absolute mass of its discrete Green sequence and establish the rigorous stability-constant bounds $23/20<Λ_3<579/500$. A causal third-order memory quadrature with nonnegative assembled weights then yields exponentially weighted stability without a parabolic step-size restriction. With third-order starting values, we prove a uniform-in-time third-order temporal error estimate and extend it to conforming finite elements. Numerical tests confirm the predicted convergence orders and the long-time behavior.

title: Cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$
abstract: A graph is edge-transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its edge set. This paper is devoted to a systematic study of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$, where $p$ is a prime and $\ell$ is an even integer. We first show that either $Γ$ is the unique cubic edge-transitive graph of order $18$, or its full automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(Γ)$ contains a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ which is isomorphic to either $Z_{p^2}$ or $Z_{p}^2$. For the case $P\cong Z_{p^2}$, we prove that $Γ$ is either arc-regular or edge-regular, and provide a complete classification of such graphs. For the case $P\cong Z_{p}^2$, we prove that $Γ$ is a normal cover of certain known graphs. This work generalizes previous classifications by Zhou and Feng (2024), Lu et al.~(2004), and others. As an application, we obtain a classification of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$ in the case where $\ell$ is square-free.

title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
abstract: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.

title: A stochastic mirror descent algorithm for mean-field control problems
abstract: We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.

title: On the Algebraic Structure of Lewis Carroll's Logic -- Behind the Looking Glass: A Mathematical Perspective
abstract:
Charles Ludwidge Dodgeson, better known by his literary pen name `Lewis Carroll', has a number of well known and cherished literary works to his credit, for example "Alice in Wonderland" and "Through the Looking Glass". Apart from this he is known to have a strong professional interest in mathematics and logic with an inclination towards an educational and recreational perspective.
  In this work we consider the algebraic structure behind Lewis Carroll's approach to classical logic and his logical puzzles. Starting with the arithmetic of $0$ and $1$, we develop the connections between Boolean-valued functions, sets and predicates, which we refer to as the "entangled trinity". This provides a common setting in which Carroll's approach and Boole's perspective can be understood. Particular attention is given to what is meant by "the conclusion" of a logical problem. We suggest a precise interpretation of a complete conclusion in terms of largest lower bounds involving only the predicates to be retained, thereby sharpening Carroll's approach. The role of natural language in choosing a suitable universe and identifying these predicates is discussed through a variety of examples. Finally, we present computerised solution methods, including the use of Boolean satisfiability solvers for larger puzzles.

title: Conway polynomials of $Th(p,q)$ and $Th(q,p)$: a proof of Takemura's conjecture
abstract:
Takemura conjectured that the Conway polynomials $\sum a_\ell z^\ell$ of the Turk's head link $Th(p,q)$ and $\sum b_\ell z^\ell$ of $Th(q,p)$ satisfy $a_\ell=b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv0,1\pmod 4$ and $a_\ell=-b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv2,3\pmod4$, and proved it for $q=2,3$. We prove it for all $p,q\ge1$, knots and links. Equivalently, $
abla_{Th(q,p)}(z)=c\,
abla_{Th(p,q)}(iz)$ with $c=1$ if $\gcd(p,q)$ is odd and $c=-i$ if it is even. The proof combines a product formula $
abla_{Th(p,q)}(z)^2=\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\prod_{k=1}^{q-1}(z^2+2\cos rac{2πk}{q}-2\cos rac{2πj}{p})$, which comes from the reduced Burau representation, with the leading coefficients, read off the Seifert surface of the closed braid.

title: Averages of traces and ratios of characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices
abstract: In this work we explore the extent to which the Ratios Theorem for averages over $U(N)$, with respect to Haar measure, of ratios of characteristic polynomials can be used to evaluate averages of traces of unitary matrices. We derive concrete expressions for all averages involving up to 4 traces, valid for any matrix size, $N$. We also calculate the so-called zero-swap and one-swap contributions to an average with any number of traces, which amounts to determining general trace moments in a range double the size of the renowned result of Diaconis and Shahshahani. The expression is tractable enough to use in applications, for example to determine the parameter range where certain trace averages assume negative values.

title: Weak-$L^\infty$ and BMO with Hausdorff Content
abstract:
The space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ on measure space was introduced by Bennett et al. (Ann. of Math., 113(1981), 601-611) and proved to contain the space of $L^\infty$ and possess the appropriate interpolation property. In this paper, we are aimed to continue this line of research on the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$ endowed with Hausdorff content, which is a low-dimensional outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and fails to be additive or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measures. But low-dimensional subsets, such as fractals, of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are Hausdorff capacitable. Precisely, in the setting of Hausdorff content, an analogue of weak-$L^\infty$ is defined and proved to possess an improved Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. Moreover, we show that the space of functions with bounded mean oscillation associated to the Hausdorff content is embedded into this new weak-$L^\infty$ space by establishing a key estimate for the distribution via a packing condition.
  As a by-product,
  the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood operator on the space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ is established.

title: A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
abstract: Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erdős and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators. Dixmier subsequently proved their conjecture $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_n^2/(n-1)$, a bound depending only on $a_n$ and $n$ that removes the factor $2$ from the corresponding quadratic estimate. Following the Erdős--Graham approach, we remove the factor $2$ while retaining the dependence on $a_{n-1}$, and prove $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_{n-1}\lceil a_n/(n-1)\rceil-a_n-1$. This bound can be substantially smaller than Dixmier's when $a_{n-1}$ is small relative to $a_n$. For every $n\ge3$, we also construct infinitely many instances satisfying the reverse inequality, which shows that the bound is sharp.

title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
abstract: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $β=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}λ_D^{-β/2}(1+O(λ_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(λ_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(λ_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schrödinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.

title: Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
abstract: Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$. We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank. In this case, $S_L/J_A$ is the toric ring obtained from Hibi's parametrization of the Hibi ring of $L$ by identifying suitable pairs of variables, and for an arbitrary $A$ we describe the saturation of $J_A$ as a lattice ideal.

title: Restricted isometries in finite-dimensional $\ell^p$-spaces
abstract: For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(ξ)\|_p=\|ξ|_E\|_p$ for every $ξ\in\ell_d^p$. We call these maps \emph{restricted isometries}. Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ. We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.

title: Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic
abstract: This paper studies foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic. We provide an explicit description of all smooth foliations, linear and turbulent, and establish criteria for being $p$-closed. We explicitly determine the moduli spaces of such foliations. We give an application to the construction of $p$-closed foliations, with mild singularities, on Kummer $K3$-surfaces in positive characteristics.

title: Rational Points on Affine Varieties over Finite Fields and Polygonal Number Sequences
abstract: Authors, in an earlier work, proved that prime power subsequences of the polygonal numbers corresponding to $4$, $6$, $8$, and $10$ arise naturally as the numbers of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of certain double Danielewski surfaces. In this work, authors generalize the previous construction and give a new family of affine varieties over finite fields such that the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of these varieties give the prime power subsequence of every polygonal number sequence.

title: Stationary bistable fronts on a periodic necklace graph: existence, stability and multiplicity
abstract: We study stationary fronts for a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with the McKean reaction on a periodic necklace metric graph. For profiles that agree on each pair of parallel edges, the problem reduces to a scalar equation on the real line with a periodic, piecewise constant diffusion coefficient. The diffusion contrast of the necklace is not small, so the coefficient cannot be treated as a small perturbation of a constant. Because the McKean reaction is piecewise linear, the equation is affine between threshold crossings and coefficient interfaces, and a front is determined explicitly by its crossing points. We find an explicit interval of reaction thresholds, the pinning interval, such that stationary fronts, monotone or not, exist exactly for thresholds in this interval. Up to translations by the spatial period, there are exactly two decreasing fronts at each interior threshold and one front at each endpoint. For each fixed interior threshold, one decreasing front is Lyapunov stable and the other is unstable in the $W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ norm, among mild solutions with one continuously moving threshold crossing. The crossing phases of the two decreasing fronts also determine nonmonotone fronts. For each interior threshold and odd $m\geq3$, choose $m$ periods of the coefficient that are sufficiently far apart. There are then exactly $2^m$ fronts with one threshold crossing in each chosen period and none elsewhere. Varying the chosen periods gives infinitely many inequivalent fronts with $m$ crossings.

title: Linear transformations of tropical matrices preserving individual values of the cyclicity index
abstract: The cyclicity index is used to study the periodic behavior of powers of tropical matrices. It is determined by the structure of the critical subgraph of a matrix, which consists of the cycles with the largest average weight. In this paper bijective linear transformations of tropical matrices that preserve an individual value $k\neq 2$ of this invariant are studied.

title: The Turán number of Berge paths in connected hypergraphs
abstract:
A Berge path in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of distinct vertices and edges $v_1,e_1, v_2, \ldots, e_{k-1}, v_{k}$ such that $v_i, v_{i+1} \in e_i$ for all $i \in [k-1]$. Győri, Katona, and Lemons determined the maximum number edges in $r$-uniform, $n$-vertex hypergraphs without Berge paths on $k$ vertices. The extremal examples for their bounds are disconnected hypergraphs in which each component has either too few edges or too few vertices to contain such a Berge path.
  We consider the setting in which the host hypergraph is connected. Let $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{conn}}_r(n,\mathcal{BP}_k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex, $r$-uniform, connected hypergraph that does not contain a Berge path on $k$ vertices. This number was determined by Zhang, Broersma, Győri, Tompkins, Wang for $k \leq r+2$, and Zhao, Gerbner, Zhou for $k \geq 2r+2$. In this paper, we resolved the remaining cases $r+3 \leq k \leq 2r+1$ when $n$ is sufficiently large, confirming a conjecture of Zhang, et al.

title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE$_3$
abstract: The scaling limits of interfaces in the critical two-dimensional Ising model are described by the Schramm--Loewner evolution $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. While, in the scaling limit, the law of the whole near-critical FK-Ising configuration is known to be singular with respect to the critical law in the thermal direction, and the same is expected for the spin configuration, we prove in this paper that the law of a single interface is not. More precisely, we consider the Ising model with mesh $δ$ in the Dobrushin square at $β=β_c-mδ$, where $m\ne0$ is fixed, and we prove that the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the law of the interface with respect to its critical law has moments of every positive and negative order, bounded uniformly in $δ$, so that the law of every subsequential scaling limit of the interface is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to that of $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. Our analysis explains the mechanism behind this result: the logarithmically growing specific heat (that is, the variance of the Hamiltonian, normalized by the number of edges) cancels between the full domain and the domain slit along the interface.

title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
abstract: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.

title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.

title: Traces of Green's functions on $\mathbb{H}^q$ over point-hypersurface pairs
abstract: The famous algebraicity conjecture of Gross and Zagier for the values at CM points of higher Green's functions was recently proven by Bruinier, Li and Yang. Motivated by this the values of the automorphic Green's function at pairs of special points in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ were studied by Herrero, Imamoglu, von Pippich and Schwagenscheidt, and an analogous algebraicity result for traces of Green's functions was established. In this paper, we consider higher automorphic Green's functions $G_{s}(P,Q)$ on hyperbolic $q$-space $\mathbb{H}^q$ for $q\geq 2$ when the spectral parameter $s$ is a positive even integer, and prove an explicit finite formula for their traces over geodesic hypersurfaces in one of the variables. This formula provides a geometric interpretation of the traces of Green's functions for every choice of a point in $\mathbb{H}^q$ for the second variable. As an application, we obtain rationality results when the second variable is evaluated at a special point providing further evidence that such results for traces of Green's functions do not depend on any underlying complex structure.

title: Instability of mean curvature flow in expander coordinates
abstract: We study rotationally symmetric graphical solutions to mean curvature flow that are initially close to a homothetic reference expander, in particular near infinity. Based on a computer algebra aided proof, we show that under appropriate conditions, at large times, the solutions are closer to a different expander than to the reference expander.

title: Beam Search for Error-Correcting Codes via Conditional Diffusion
abstract: We introduce a diffusion framework for neural decoding of error-correcting codes (ECCs). We interpret decoding as a conditional diffusion process that progressively predicts codeword bits while treating the physical channel observation as fixed side information. At each stage, a neural model estimates bitwise posteriors conditioned on the physical observation and the current noisy state of the codeword. We focus particularly on masked diffusion, for which the reverse process naturally induces a Maxwell beam search (MBS) procedure inspired by the Maxwell construction of Measson et al. Rather than committing to a single uncertain decision, the decoder maintains multiple candidate trajectories, removes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks the remaining candidates using accumulated reverse-transition log-probabilities. We evaluate the framework across multiple code families on binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Experiments show competitive decoding performance across Polar, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes. The MBS decoder consistently improves upon the corresponding single-trajectory diffusion decoder and, in all evaluated settings, improves upon available neural decoding results.

title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges. This resolves the weighted proximity conjecture by Hörsch, Imolay, Mizutani, Oki, and Schwarcz. Our main technical tool is to replace the assumption of Schrijver--Seymour Conjecture in Liu and Xu's earlier work with Kemperman--Scherk Theorem. The proximity theorem combined with approaches in earlier work gives an FPT algorithm that finds a min-cost $F$-avoiding base parameterized by $|G|$. We additionally give an FPT algorithm parameterized by $|F|$, answering a question of Hörsch et al.

title: AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length $L$ and age threshold $T$ satisfy $L\ge T>N\ge2$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.

title: The restricted Hurwitz action on cameral decompositions of Coxeter elements
abstract: Given a dual Coxeter system (W, T) of rank n, the Hurwitz action of the braid group on the reduced T-decompositions of a Coxeter element is transitive. When we choose a geometric representation of W, the reflections with respect to the n walls of one given chamber form a generating set S that we call cameral. An ordering of S is called a cameral decomposition and the product a cameral Coxeter element, which depends only on the quiver obtained by orienting the Coxeter diagram with vertices S according to the ordering. We show that the reduced decompositions of a cameral Coxeter elements for which the underlying set S satisfies that (W, S ) is a Coxeter system, are necessarily cameral, and we count the number of chambers from which a cameral Coxeter element can be obtained. We show that one can go through all these chambers using the restricted Hurwitz action on the set of cameral decompositions, which is generated by transpositions of adjacent commuting reflections and by the Garside element δ of the dual Garside structure, which acts by a quiver mutation of the orientation of the Coxeter diagram.

title: Polarization on Bounded Euclidean Spaces and More General Compact Groups
abstract: We establish polarization for memoryless sources taking values on the unit-perimeter circle, or on more general compact groups, under Arıkan's polar transform. For sources with finite differential entropy, all but an $O((\log N)^{-1/12})$ fraction of the conditional differential entropies in successive cancellation order lie within any fixed positive distance of zero, where $N$ is the block length. Examples indicate that the true polarization rate is indeed very slow: an inverse-logarithmic rate does not underestimate the polarization speed at moderate block lengths.

title: G-ORACLE: A Fast Geometric Method To Explore All Near-Optimal Designs for Energy Systems
abstract:
Modeling to Generate Alternatives (MGA) methods explore the near-optimal solutions of energy system optimization models (ESOMs), i.e., alternative planning pathways whose cost lies within a small predefined slack of the optimum but which can differ substantially in technology composition, regional distribution, and environmental impacts. Among MGA methods, ORACLE uniquely guarantees convergence to the near-optimal set within a targeted tolerance by iteratively refining inner and outer polytope approximations. At each iteration, given a trial point, it solves a problem as hard as the ESOM to find the nearest near-optimal solution to it. However, the trial point is obtained by solving a bilevel problem whose solution time grows rapidly with the number of iterations and eventually dominates the computational cost of the method.
  To eliminate this bottleneck, we present G-ORACLE, which exploits the fact that an optimal solution of the bilevel problem is always attained at a vertex of the outer approximation. G-ORACLE therefore replaces the bilevel problem with incremental vertex enumeration by the double description method and one convex projection per vertex, while retaining the convergence guarantee of ORACLE. A supporting-hyperplane check further avoids unnecessary recomputation of these projections as the inner approximation grows.
  We evaluate G-ORACLE on an electricity-only PyPSA-Eur model, exploring the near-optimal space of the installed capacities of six generation and two storage technologies. While ORACLE's bilevel problem exceeds 20 minutes at iteration 64, G-ORACLE performs the trial-point search in at most 14 seconds throughout 240 iterations, leaving the ESOM solves as the only significant computational cost.

title: A Proximal Gradient Method for Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization with Applications
abstract: We study a proximal-gradient method for the sum of a convex smooth function $g$ and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth, strongly quasar-convex regularizer. The gradient step is weighted by the quasar-convexity parameter, so, for step sizes in the descent range, the iteration decreases a weighted objective, while the unweighted sum serves for comparison. We establish a geometric envelope around every global minimizer of the unweighted objective, with an explicit radius independent of the step size; a common minimizer yields global linear convergence. We also prove that every critical point $u$ of the weighted objective lies within an explicit multiple of $\|\nabla g(u)\|$ from every global minimizer of the unweighted objective. Together with an optimized composite comparison, this yields asymptotic distance bounds. An example shows that the two objectives can have different critical points. For power-regularized least squares with powers between zero and one, descent provides a confinement ball for the sharp local modulus, and support identification combined with a KL argument yields whole-sequence convergence.

title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_φ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

title: Counting curves with bounded intersection
abstract: This paper counts curves, and multicurves, on hyperbolic surfaces, providing explicit upper bounds that depend polynomially on length and exponentially in terms of an upper bound on self-intersection.

title: Superlinear Convergence of Cyclic Gradient Methods with Historical Ritz Step Sizes
abstract: Simplified spectral models predict dimension-dependent superlinear convergence for gradient methods, but the corresponding behavior of actual iterations remains only partially understood. Historical methods introduce an additional difficulty: the gradients defining the step sizes differ from those receiving them. We study this offset for cyclic reuse of historical Ritz step sizes on strictly convex quadratics. Within the existing limited memory steepest descent with retards (LMSDR) family, a rolling cyclic Ritz (RCR) rule reuses $m$ historical Ritz values $\ell$ times per cycle, ending with a complete sweep. At $q=m+1$ active distinct eigenvalues, an exact delayed recurrence gives almost-everywhere doubly exponential convergence with an explicit rate and exceptional weights. Nonempty open basins also exist for $m+1<q\le2m$ and $\ell\ge4$. Rebuilding the history from each cycle-start gradient costs $m$ additional updates and gives sampled cyclic Ritz reuse (SCR) a cycle-end map determined by the current weights. Under uniform sampling bounds, SCR converges doubly exponentially almost everywhere when $(2\ell-1)^m>\binom{q-1}{m}$. Increasing $\ell$ admits larger $q$ for fixed $m$. The guarantee extends to history-dependent choices from finite sampling menus under a bound on the number of admissible sampling sequences. Geometrically spaced decisions retain the SCR condition and rate range. Every update is counted, including sampling; a numerical illustration compares finite-tolerance update counts.

title: Regret-Based Scenario-Tree Construction for Multistage Stochastic Programs with Deterministic Constraints
abstract:
Scenario trees are widely used to discretize multistage stochastic programs into forms that are tractable for numerical optimization. Yet, traditional scenario-tree construction methods are typically based on statistical similarity between the original uncertainty process and its discretization, and may fail to preserve the aspects of the uncertainty that matter most for decision-making.
  This paper shows that, under a fixed probability measure and deterministic feasibility constraints, the gap between the optimal value of the original multistage stochastic program and that of its scenario-tree approximation decomposes exactly into a sum of nodewise regret terms, each measuring the optimality loss at a particular node. This decomposition provides a clear target for scenario-tree construction: minimizing total regret across the tree. Motivated by this result, we propose a practical two-phase construction method for repeated stochastic optimization. In an offline phase, computationally inexpensive surrogates for decision regret are learned from data, and in the online phase, these surrogates guide scenario-tree construction. The resulting framework retains the structured optimization and constraint-handling capabilities of multistage stochastic programming while exploiting learned information about the uncertainty to make more effective use of a limited scenario-tree budget.
  Numerical experiments on multistage stochastic storage and production-planning problems show that, for a fixed tree size, the proposed method constructs higher-quality scenario trees and achieves better closed-loop performance than traditional scenario-tree construction methods.

title: The Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic for primes $p$ and $p+4$ from a uniform zeta-ratios conjecture
abstract: We prove the Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of difference four from a restricted uniform two-over-two zeta-ratios formula. The formula has error $O_\varepsilon(U^{1/2+\varepsilon})$, real parts of all four shifts in $[3/64,5/64]$, and imaginary parts of absolute value at most $U^{1/4}$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,101/100)$, we obtain an error $O_\varepsilon(x^{-1/16+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_\varepsilon(x^{-3/8+\varepsilon})$. The proof retains the crossed zero residues in Mellin inversion and estimates their mixed term with the logarithmic-derivative integral. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference four. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_4$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted Möbius approximant in the Nyman--Beurling criterion by finite identities.

title: Necessary and Sufficient Criteria for Global PID Regulation of Nonlinear Uncertain System
abstract: Although classical PID control is widely used in engineering practice, identifying all PID gains that guarantee global regulation of nonlinear uncertain dynamics remains challenging. For a class of second-order nonaffine systems under one-sided derivative bounds, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global PID regulation: a fixed PID controller globally regulates the entire infinite-dimensional uncertainty class if and only if it regulates a single boundary linear system. Applying the Routh--Hurwitz criterion to this boundary linear system yields the exact admissible PID gain region. To establish this equivalence, we prove a structured Markus--Yamabe theorem for third-order integrator chains under uniform derivative-ratio conditions. Its proof combines a two-dimensional storage function constructed via viscosity solutions of a Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a scalar comparison argument. We further show that the same PID gain region remains exact for multidimensional affine systems under symmetry assumptions on the state partial Jacobians and the input matrix.

title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $Ξ$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
abstract: We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|κ|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $κ$. Fixed-point irrationality and exact Picard rank remain open. The heat tangent differs from the matched fixed-exponent isomonodromic direction, but admits a local moving-exponent curve lift. Separately, a reciprocal-head canopy certificate combined with published finite-RH and rectangular time-barrier verifications bounds the de Bruijn--Newman constant by $Λ\le433/2500=0.1732$ without a QRH assumption. These local arithmetic and global analytic results share a phase--transverse bridge; no equivalence between core nonresonance and RH is asserted.

title: Avalanches of the Abelian sandpile on the hierarchical lattice
abstract: We study the Abelian sandpile model on a sequence of finite fractal graphs: the hierarchical, or Migdal--Kadanoff, lattices. Our first main result consists of matching power-law tail bounds for the avalanche and the uniform wave started at certain "pivotal" vertices. We also establish a limiting result for the pivotal reach of the avalanche and, finally, a scaling limit for the size of a uniform wave started at a vertex of high degree.

title: How much do increasing events occur disjointly?
abstract: We establish two general quantitative lower bounds on the gap in the classical BK inequality for increasing events. The first is an analogue of Talagrand's quantitative FKG inequality (1996) and depends on the influences. The second is specific to the BK inequality and involves both the influences and the probabilities of symmetric disjoint pivots.

title: Hot Spots: From Smooth to Nonsmooth Simply Connected Planar Domains
abstract: Assuming the absence of interior local extrema for first positive Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded smooth simply connected planar domains, as reported in \cite{SmoothInput}, we extend the hot spots conclusion to simply connected domains of finite area with compact Sobolev embedding and simple first positive Neumann eigenvalue. The supremum and infimum are approached in arbitrarily thin boundary layers. For bounded domains and eigenfunctions continuous up to the boundary, both extrema are attained on the boundary. We also transfer polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bounds uniformly along a conformal exhaustion and construct explicit bounded and unbounded examples, including domains with cusps and a domain with infinitely many corners and bottlenecks. Some of these examples admit no polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bound.

title: Variance of relative entropy over random states
abstract: Average relative entropy over major generic random states is recently studied. In this work, the investigation is extended by deriving the variances of relative entropy over the Hilbert--Schmidt and Bures--Hall ensembles, which characterize its fluctuations around the average value. Exact results for the variances of relative entropy between independent states drawn from the same ensemble and from two different ensembles are obtained. These results further indicate that the average relative entropy is typical in the considered limiting regimes. In addition to the matrix-level calculations similar to the average relative entropy, eigenvalue correlation functions of the ensembles are involved in the variance computations through the use of zonal polynomials.

title: From entropy waves to vortex sheets for the Euler equations
abstract: We construct piecewise smooth solutions of the full compressible Euler equations that evolve from entropy waves into vortex sheets while retaining a strictly positive Taylor jump. For every integer $κ\geq1$, we obtain solutions satisfying initial material compatibility for pressure and velocity through order $κ$, whose tangential velocity jump has a nonzero leading term of order $t^{κ+1}$. These solutions are periodic in the tangential variables and admit a smooth realization in a slab with impermeable walls. We also construct solutions on a local nonperiodic tangential patch that satisfy initial material compatibility at every order, yet have a tangential velocity jump that is nonzero for every sufficiently small positive time and flat at $t=0$. The finite-order construction uses a normal Cauchy-Kowalevski problem for velocity potentials, whereas the all-order construction uses a homogeneous reduction to a smooth hyperbolic Cauchy problem.

title: A Short Proof of Zhang's Conjecture on Stack-Sortable Permutations
abstract: We give a short proof of Zhang's conjecture that the number of stack-sortable permutations of length $n + 1$ which end in their smallest element is equal to the $n$-th Motzkin number.

title: Logarithmic Separation between LZ77 and LZ-End and Grammar Compression
abstract: We show that there is a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End, and between LZ77 and grammar compression.

title: Numerical analysis of a Lax-Wendroff type lattice Boltzmann scheme for the advection equation
abstract: A linear monodimensional lattice Boltzmann scheme with three velocities tackling the advection equation is investigated. We prove that it is second-order accurate and provide necessary and sufficient stability conditions through an explicit formula involving the two relaxation parameters. Relying on existing results for finite difference schemes, we prove convergence for smooth initial data with initialization of the non-conserved moments at equilibrium. Several numerical simulations illustrate these theoretical findings.

title: On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
abstract: Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.

title: Veering triangulations of once-punctured torus bundles are unique
abstract: We show that each hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundle has exactly one veering triangulation. We also find manifolds for which the exact number of veering structures is known and is greater than one. Finally, we give new examples of manifolds without veering triangulations.

title: Neural network enhancement of the Born approximation
abstract: We examine the use of neural networks in conjunction with the Born approximation for solving the inverse scattering problem for a penetrable medium in the frequency domain. The goal is a fast method for determining the refractive index of a scatterer from multistatic far-field measurements at one frequency. We present a new neural network model that seeks to improve on our previous results in by sharpening the reconstructed images. In addition, we present two other networks motivated by the corrected Born method that avoid the need to invert the regularized Born operator. These latter algorithms will be important for future three dimensional applications when the inverse Born approximation is difficult to compute, or when near-field measurements are used. Computational results illustrate that the new corrections to the Born approximation can provide an accurate and flexible approach to the inverse scattering problem.

title: Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem
abstract: We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.

title: Bistability with equal and independent removal in small bimolecular networks
