abstract: We classify two-species mass-action networks with at most three internal directed reactions on $\{X,Y,2X,X+Y,2Y\}$, positive inflows, and linear removal of both species. Among the 681 networks up to species exchange, exactly 27 admit two distinct positive hyperbolic attracting equilibria. The same 27 admit bistability with equal removal rates and with independently chosen positive removal rates. Each is minimal under reaction deletion. We give rational equal-removal witnesses for all positive cases and all-parameter exclusions for the remaining 654. The proof combines nullcline geometry, polynomial sign tests, resultant root bounds, and exact flux-cone decompositions. A separate rational-arithmetic implementation verifies the complete classification and its equilibrium certificates.

title: A complete Kähler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
abstract: We construct complete smooth Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the Kähler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.

title: Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics
abstract: We consider the left translation action of an element $a$ on a finite-volume semisimple homogeneous space $G/Γ$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(a)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb{R}$. Assuming exponential mixing, we prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for compactly supported smooth test functions. As an application, we prove effective uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy. We also obtain quantitative pointwise equidistribution for Haar-almost every point on each full expanding horosphere.

title: Non-equilibrium density fluctuations for the stirring process with weak boundary dynamics
abstract: We consider the one-dimensional stirring process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We investigate the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the system, starting from a product measure associated with a smooth initial profile. The limit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is given in terms of the Laplacian and gradient operators acting on test functions satisfying time-dependent Robin boundary conditions that are obtained by linearizing the boundary conditions in the hydrodynamic equation. A central ingredient in our analysis is the derivation of sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree for the centered occupation variables; these bounds were proved in the companion article \cite{birmpa2025nonequilibriumfluctuationsstirringprocess}.

title: Sharp asymmetric vertex-Ramsey properties of graphs
abstract: In 1992, Łuczak, Ruciński and Voigt showed that for any graph $H$, a parameter $m_1(H)$ - called the 1-density - governs the threshold at which the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ inherits the vertex-Ramsey property. In 2000, Friedgut and Krivelevich showed this threshold is sharp for graphs satisfying a natural balancedness condition. In 1996, Kreuter showed that for any graphs $H_1, \ldots, H_r$ with $m_1(H_1) \geq \cdots \geq m_1(H_r)$, a parameter dependent only on $H_1$ and $H_2$ governs the threshold at which $G(n,p)$ inherits the `asymmetric' vertex-Ramsey property. We prove this threshold is sharp for graphs respecting natural balancedness conditions, including in the analogous hypergraph setting.

title: Properties and applications of Muckenhoupt $A_1$ growth weights
abstract:
For $β\ge0$, let $A_1^{(β)}$ be the class of weights satisfying $$
  [w]_{A_1^{(β)}}:=
  \sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1}
  \varepsilon^β[w]_{A_{1+\varepsilon}}<\infty. $$ These classes satisfy $A_1\subsetneq A_1^{(β)}\subsetneq\bigcap_{p>1}A_p$ for $β>0$. For every $α\ge0$, we prove that $w\in A_1^{(β)}$ if and only if $$ w\left(\left\{M_{L(\log L)^α}f>λ\right\}\right) \le C\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{|f(x)|}λ \left[ \log\left(e+\frac{|f(x)|}λ\right) \right]^{α+β} w(x)\,\mathrm{d}x.
  $$ The least constant $C$ is comparable to $[w]_{A_1^{(β)}}$. Also, we obtain corresponding characterizations for Calderón--Zygmund operators and their commutators.

title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.

title: A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum
abstract: We consider a supercritical two-type continuous-time linear birth-death process with mutation and selection, in which wild-type individuals give rise to mutant offspring with a larger net-growth rate. We previously had obtained first-order law of large number results for the driver site frequency spectrum. We return to obtain a second-order central limit theorem, in which we show stable convergence of a scaling of the deviation of the SFS from its first-order limit. We provide a central limit theorem at both large detection times and sizes. Then, we apply these results to obtain confidence intervals for a class of consistent estimators for the fitness advance.

title: Rank 3 curve semistable Higgs bundles: the nilpotent case
abstract: A Higgs bundle on a smooth complex projective variety is curve semistable if its pullback to every smooth projective curve is semistable. A 2008 conjecture asserts that this is equivalent to slope semistability for some polarization plus vanishing discriminant. One direction is known, the converse holds in rank two, and Huang recently gave a rank-four counterexample. We prove the conjecture for rank three nilpotent Higgs bundles in any dimension. We treat separately the two possible cases: if the Higgs field $φ$ is nilpotent of order two, there is a divisorial component of a Higgs Grassmannian where nefness of the normalized tautological class forces the discriminant to vanish; otherwise, $φ$ is regular nilpotent, and then the canonical kernel flag, commutativity and Bogomolov's lemma on line subbundles of the cotangent bundle complete the proof.

title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
abstract: Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $η\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\leη\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons. In this work we solve this variational problem for every $η\in(0,1)$. We show that every minimizer is either a constant graphon or a step graphon with two blocks of equal size. Correspondingly, the conditioned graph is close to an Erdős-Rényi graph or to a symmetric stochastic block model with two blocks. These two regimes are separated by a first order phase transition at the threshold $η_*=0.009217\ldots$. This resolves a conjecture of Zhao [78] and an open problem of Janson and Warnke [39] on triangles. It thereby gives a complete description of the lower tail of triangle counts in this range of $p$.

title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
abstract: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

title: Triangle-Free Sets in Exact-Distance Hamming Graphs
abstract:
Let $T_q(n,r)$ be the largest size of a vertex set inducing a triangle-free subgraph of the graph on $[q]^n$ whose edges join words at Hamming distance $r$. We study this quantity for fixed alphabet size and fixed distance, with particular emphasis on the ternary cube. Alphabet restriction transfers the binary fixed-distance theorem of Balogh, Chen, and Li to give $T_q(n,2h)=O_h(q^n/n^h)$. We extend the known distance-one formula and distance-two order to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, obtaining $T_q(n,1)=2q^{n-1}$ and $T_q(n,2)=Θ_q(q^n/n)$, and establish $T_3(n,4)=Θ(3^n/n^2)$. For general fixed distance, we prove \[
  T_q(n,r)=Ω_{q,r}\!\left(
  \frac{q^n\sqrt{\log n}}{n^{(r+\lfloor r/2\rfloor)/2}}
  \right)\qquad(q\ge3), \] while we show that $T_q(n,r)=Ω_{q,r}(q^n/n^{\lfloor(q-1)r/q\rfloor})$ holds for prime-power $q$ and $r\ge2$ via the extended BCH parity-check constructions. At distance three, we construct coordinate weights avoiding bounded-coefficient three-term relations and obtain \[ T_q(n,3)\ge q^n/[n\exp(O_q(\sqrt{\log n}))]. \] Our main ternary construction combines cap partitions, multicolor triangle Ramsey colorings, and a quadratic map to obtain \[
  T_3(n,3)=Ω\!\left(
  \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\,3^n\right). \] A coordinate-line counting argument gives the complementary upper bound $T_3(n,3)\le(5/27+O(n^{-1}))3^n$, together with an explicit bound for every fixed $q\ge3$. Whether the ternary density tends to zero remains open.

title: Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups
abstract: We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric. To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special. The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group. This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.

title: The totally nonnegative wonderful compactification of G is a ball
abstract: Let $\overline{G}$ denote the wonderful compactification of a semisimple algebraic group $G$ of adjoint type. We use contractive flows to show that the totally nonnegative part of every $G \times G$ orbit closure of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In particular, the totally nonnegative part of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed ball.

title: The Verra involution on special cubic fourfolds
abstract: We present a detailed study of the Hodge theory, geometry and derived categories of Verra fourfolds, and their relationship with twisted K3 surfaces and cubic fourfolds. We classify Brauer classes of Verra type on K3 surfaces of degree 2, and use this to derive an explicit counting formula for Fourier--Mukai partners of a large class of Verra fourfolds. We develop the basic theory of cohomology of Verra fourfolds and apply it to prove a derived Torelli theorem for a large class of Verra fourfolds. As an application, we prove that L-equivalent Verra fourfolds in this class are Fourier--Mukai partners, and conjecture that this implication holds for all Verra fourfolds. We then give a construction of cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. The construction yields examples of cubic and Verra fourfolds whose associated twisted K3 surfaces have non-trivial Brauer classes. Therefore, these fourfolds are expected to be irrational.

title: Modified scattering for the 3D Hartree equation with singular external potentials
abstract: We establish modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Coulomb interaction and singular external potentials, including repulsive Coulomb and inverse-square potentials. In the defocusing case, the result holds for arbitrary initial data in $H^{0,1}(\mathbb R^3)\cap H^{1,0}(\mathbb R^3)$. In particular, we obtain large-data modified scattering for the flat defocusing Hartree equation. For the focusing problem with repulsive Coulomb potential $V(x)=κ|x|^{-1}$, we prove radial modified scattering under the sharp mass condition $|λ|\|u_0\|_2^2\leq 2κ$, including the endpoint, and construct standing waves at every larger mass. Our argument obtains strong $L^2$ convergence from rescaled energy and comparison with a frozen-field evolution.

title: Vertex operator algebra realizations of untwisted Haagerup--Izumi centers
abstract:
For every odd integer $N\geq3$, we construct an untwisted Haagerup--Izumi fusion category $\mathcal H_N$ on the negative spherical branch and a simple, self-contragredient, regular, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra $E_N$ of central charge $-16N$, together with an equivalence of modular fusion categories: \[
  \operatorname{Rep}(E_N)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_N). \]
  The VOA $E_N$ is rational, has exactly $N^2+3$ irreducible modules, and is lower bounded and integer graded, with least conformal degree $-(N-1)/2$. The proof begins with a CFT-type cyclic Virasoro extension of central charge $-5N$, whose regularity we establish. Two categorical condensations recover $\mathcal H_N$, and a finite extension by shifted lattice modules removes the auxiliary pointed factor. We identify the complete ribbon modular data of $Z(\mathcal H_N)$ with $\mathrm{MD}_{-}(\mathbb Z/N;\mathbb Z/(N^2+4),b\mapsto b^2/(N^2+4))$ in the notation of Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav, for every odd $N$.

title: Lacunary maximal operators on convex boundaries
abstract: We disprove the cap-sufficiency proposal in Wright's Problem 16 for $1<p<(\sqrt{13}-1)/2$ and for $p>3$. For each fixed exponent in these ranges, one smooth strictly convex domain has finite original directional cap integral, while the lacunary maximal operator of complete arclength fails restricted weak type. We also give a geometric sufficient condition for strong $L^p$ boundedness, for every finite $1<p<\infty$, on an arbitrary given bounded convex domain. It requires one logarithmic integral of a curvature lower envelope, without a differentiability assumption on the boundary or a restriction on the number of curvature zeros. Both results concern unnormalised true arclength, one fixed interior origin and all integer dyadic dilations.

title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
abstract: We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan. We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan. We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.

title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
abstract: We consider a near-critical version of loop-erased random walk (LERW) by boosting the weight of the underlying random walk according to its length before loop-erasure. We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=π^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.

title: Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures
abstract: We prove sharp bounds for the upper and lower intermediate dimensions of orthogonal and radial projections of compactly supported measures. Both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension. We obtain exceptional-set estimates using the entire source dimension function, with sharpness for explicit families. We also construct a fixed measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open direction sets, even when all source dimensions lie below the target dimension.

title: A probabilistic construction of maximum $h$-scattered subspaces
abstract: Let $1\le h\le n-2$ and $g=\gcd(n,h+1)$. We prove that, for every prime power $q$, a maximum $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ exists whenever $(h+1)\mid rn$ and $$r\ge\frac{h+1}{g}\bigl(h(n-h-2)+1\bigr).$$ In particular, for fixed $n$ and minimum distance $δ\in\{2,\ldots,n-1\}$, $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-linear MRD codes of length $N$ exist for every $q$ and every sufficiently large $N$ such that $n$ divides $(n-δ+1)N$, with a bound on $N$ depending only on $n$ and $δ$. We take the $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-span of the columns of a random matrix $A$ over the algebra $R=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$, for a suitable $s$. Such a subspace is maximum $h$-scattered if and only if the kernel of $A$ contains no nonzero vector whose expansion with respect to an $\mathbb{F}_q$-basis of $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ has rank weight at most $h+1$. When $\gcd(n,s)=1$, $R$ is a field, and a first-moment argument, counting these vectors up to multiplication by $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^*\mathbb{F}_{q^s}^*$, shows that with positive probability the kernel contains none of them if $s>h(n-h-2)$. When $d=\gcd(n,s)>1$, $R$ is a product of $d$ fields, and vectors vanishing in some factors lie in the kernel with larger probability. We control them by proving that, for an $(h+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $D$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, the elements of $D\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ vanishing outside $k$ given factors, $0<k<d$, form an $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-space of dimension at most $(h+1)k/d$, with equality only if $D$ is linear over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ larger than $\mathbb{F}_q$. Taking $s=gr/(h+1)$ gives the bound on $r$. Finally, if $(n-h-1)\mid(h+1)$, then for every $r$ satisfying the above inequality there is an $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ of dimension $\lfloor rn/(h+1)\rfloor$, without a divisibility condition on $rn$.

title: Simple homotopy types of smooth four-manifolds with finite fundamental group
abstract: We construct closed smooth $4$-manifolds with finite fundamental group which are homotopy equivalent but not simple homotopy equivalent, even after taking a connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$. Our explicit examples have remarkably large fundamental groups; in particular, the smallest examples we obtain have fundamental groups of order roughly $10^{10^{42}}$.

title: Spectral convergence associated with Weil's quadratic form
abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study a distinguished self-adjoint extension of the differentiation operator on a Hilbert space defined by the Weil quadratic form localized to a finite interval. The local quadratic form is determined by data from finitely many places, without requiring the zeros of the Riemann zeta function as input. We prove that the positive eigenvalues of this extension converge to the distinct positive ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function as the interval expands. We also prove that the associated normalized spectral entire functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane to the canonical product over these distinct ordinates. The key step is an identity expressing the inverse of the local extension as a compression of the inverse of a global self-adjoint operator.

title: Random nodes with positive weights: Richter-Tchakaloff rules and optimal positive quadrature
abstract: We show that independent random points support exact quadrature rules with positive weights. For any $n$-dimensional space $V$ of integrable functions a constant multiple of $n\log n$ points sampled from a suitable density yields, with high probability, positive weights which integrate the functions in the space exactly. The weights stay close to the natural importance sampling weights according to the Lewis density with respect to $V$. They are the result of a weight adaptation procedure which requires an explicit $L_1$-norm discretization result that is proved on the way. As an application, we study numerical integration in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. Combining the random rules with a subsampling step, we show that positive quadrature rules with constantly oversampled nodes achieve the best possible worst-case error bound in terms of the singular numbers of the embedding into $L_2$.

title: Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups
abstract: We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$. Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation. It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups. In contrast, it turns out that the answer for dihedral groups is erratic.

title: The Lie algebra structure of $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ for blocks with a normal defect group
abstract: It is an open question whether the Lie algebra $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ of a block of a finite group algebra $kG$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of prime characteristic $p$ is simple only if the block is nilpotent with an elementary abelian defect group of order at least $3$. We show this to be the case if $B$ has a normal abelian defect group. Another open question is whether $\mathrm{HH}^1(kS_n)$ is a solvable Lie algebra, where $S_n$ denotes a symmetric group on $n$ letters. We give some general solvability criteria for $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ of blocks $B$ with a normal defect group, and, making use of results of Chuang-Kessar and Chuang-Rouquier, we deduce that if $B$ is a block of a symmetric group algebra with an abelian defect group, then $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is solvable.

title: Sharpness transitions for weighted Triebel--Lizorkin Hardy inequalities with p < q
abstract: For fractional difference energies with two power weights and distinct inner and outer exponents, we determine regimes in which the constant generated by the homogeneous power is optimal and regimes in which it loses optimality. In the range $1<p<q$, we prove sharp Hardy inequalities on nontrivial weight intervals for every sign of $D=d+2β-sp$, including a two-sided interval in the balanced case $D=0$. For $q\ge2$, these intervals extend strictly beyond an elementary pointwise scalar criterion. For $1<p<q<2$, we determine the optimal power exponent in the scalar supporting-line inequality and obtain a larger explicit sharpness interval. The proof pairs opposite logarithmic displacements and controls the nonlinear deficit by a quadratic reference energy of the transformed function. Its translation estimate allows a positive contribution at bounded scales to absorb negative contributions at remote scales. Concentrating tests prove strict loss of homogeneous sharpness near both finite-energy endpoints, and angular variations give concrete bounds for the first sharpness threshold. We extend the method to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, retaining the distinction between ambient finite-energy conditions and finiteness of the homogeneous candidate. We also treat the complementary order $p>q$, including flat-subspace inequalities and a complete alternative proof for point singularities. All sharpness sequences belong to the specified smooth test classes, and every positive optimal constant extends to their completion in the difference norm.

title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
abstract: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.

title: Total eight-colorings of maximal planar graphs of maximum degree six
abstract: We prove that every finite simple maximal planar graph of maximum degree at most six admits a total eight-coloring. We first show that every proper vertex four-coloring of a subcubic graph extends to a total five-coloring. A curvature inequality for boundary walks then gives a matching decomposition of four-connected triangulations with degrees five and six, extending their prescribed vertex four-colorings to total eight-colorings. In a minimum counterexample, two local boundary colorings force the degree-four vertices to have disjoint neighborhoods. A characterization of the local extension obstructions permits these vertices to be restored simultaneously. The proof uses Hamiltonian-connectedness of four-connected planar graphs and the computer-assisted Four-Color Theorem; it requires no further computation.

title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
abstract:
We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$
  -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0
  \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

title: The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
abstract: We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.

title: Weighted decoupling inequalities via fractal bilinear Kakeya estimates
abstract: Decoupling inequalities for the parabola are obtained for weights in physical space. The decoupling iteration relies on a fractal bilinear Kakeya estimate. We record applications to exponential sums.

title: Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
abstract: We give a probabilistic approach to the ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model. The model is formally described by the density $\exp(α\int \mathopen{:} \cos(βX) \mathclose{:} )$, where $X$ is a log-correlated Gaussian field. Our construction applies on bounded convex domains for every particle activity $α\in\mathbb R$ and throughout the subcritical range $β^2\in[0,4)$, below the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless threshold. We apply the martingale method introduced by Lacoin, Rhodes and Vargas to two dimensions by using refined estimates based on charge conjugation symmetries. Our result extends existing constructions by treating the full subcritical regime for a broad class of covariances.

title: A direct proof of the equivalence of the A2 and the Helson--Szego conditions
abstract: We give a direct proof of the equivalence between the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ and the Helson--Szegő conditions on the unit circle $T$. A positive weight $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}_2(T)$ if and only if $\log w=u+Hv$, where $u,v$ are real bounded functions, $\|v\|_\infty<\fracπ{2}$, and $H$ denotes the periodic Hilbert transform. The classical proof combines the Helson--Szegő theorem with the Hunt--Muckenhoupt--Wheeden characterization of weighted boundedness of the Hilbert transform. Our proof derives the Helson--Szegő representation directly from the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ condition, without using boundedness of $H$ on $L^2(w)$.

title: Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) direct coverage toward moving user equipment (UE), but practical deployments involve discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and UE mobility, which require the problem to be re-solved continually. We consider these challenges for the chamfered hexagonal polyhedral RIS, which provides nearly uniform coverage. With both incidence and departure angles, we bound in closed form the gain loss of its best facet relative to the best possible reflecting facet, include the known b-bit quantization loss, and extend the bound to joint random mounting errors of all facets. For a precoded multi-user downlink, each facet-selection subproblem of the max-min rate design is shown to be an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, suited to repeated time-constrained solving. The deployment of the base station in relation to the RIS allows the polyhedral surface to bring down the percentage of dead zones in vertical planar panels from 77% to 0.3% and increase the minimum rate by 34% relative to the STAR panel. The simulated annealing algorithm finds the optimum solution in 95% of the cases. The quantum approximation algorithm fails to do so.

title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollobás and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Gutiérrez, Bernués, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollobás and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

title: Correlation-induced suppression of Granger causality and Gaussian transfer entropy
abstract: In complex dynamical systems, Granger causality and transfer entropy are widely used to infer directional interactions, but they quantify a source's unique predictive contribution after conditioning and can therefore be substantially attenuated by correlation with the retained variables. Here, using our previously developed Linear Operator Causality Analysis (LOCA) framework, which measures causal response from the system propagator, we derive a relationship between predictive and operator-based causality. For a two-dimensional linear system, the fractional suppression of Granger causality equals the squared correlation between source and receiver. We generalize this result to high-dimensional systems using the source covariance remaining after conditioning and show that additional conditioning can only increase the suppression. The same covariance ordering yields a corresponding upper bound for Gaussian transfer entropy. A linearized Burgers advection chain exhibits 36.6% suppression at the convective travel-time peak, and exact nonlinear acoustic Burgers solutions show that the fitted-surrogate penalty is governed by correlation structure rather than nonlinearity and remains robust to sensor noise after operator debiasing. Applied to resting-state fMRI from the Human Connectome Project (80 brain regions, 8 functional networks, 10 subjects), the single-lag Granger causality measure falls 39.4% below the operator response when conditioning only on the receiver and 73.0% when conditioning on the receiver and all other retained variables. The framework provides a quantitative bridge between predictive and operator-based causal measures in high-dimensional dynamical systems.

title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
abstract: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $α$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($α= 0)$ and the SQG equation $(α= 1)$. We prove that, for every $α\in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$.

title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
abstract: We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus. Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a<b<c<d$, with $h=1$ when no such occurrence exists. We show that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q^h+q^{h+1}$ if exactly one of the patterns $3412$ and $4231$ occurs, and $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q+q^h$ if both patterns occur. In the latter case, $h>1$. This proves the irreducible singular locus case of a 2009 conjecture of Billey and Weed.

title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
abstract: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.

authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
title: Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals
abstract: The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=\varphi(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(\varphi,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a Möbius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.
